content: Fact Check: Old Video of Mamata Banerjee Protesting Over Fuel Prices... A video of West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee driving a scooter is being widely shared on social media. Sharing this video, users claim that the entire road was closed to teach the Bengal CM how to drive a scooter and the entire administration was helping her.The video is shared on Facebook with a Hindi caption: “ममता बनर्जी को स्कूटी सिखाने के लिए पूरी सड़क बंद कर दी और पूरा शासन स्कूटी सिखाने में लगा है ऐसे ही नेताओ ने देश को बर्बाद किया है” (English translation: The whole road was closed to teach Mamata Banerjee how to ride a scooter and the whole administration is busy in teaching her. Such leaders have ruined the country.)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, and found it to be MISLEADING.Using the InVid Tool, we extracted keyframes from the viral video and performed a Reverse Image Search. This search directed us to a news report, published by The Economic Times on February 25, 2021, that carried similar visuals of Banerjee driving a scooter. The article headline reads: “Watch: Mamata Banerjee nearly falls while driving an electric scooter to protest fuel price hike”The video was also uploaded by ANI on February 25, 2021, with the caption: “West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee nearly falls while driving an electric scooter in Howrah, as a mark of protest against the fuel price hike. She quickly regained her balance with support and continued to drive. She is travelling to Kalighat from State Secretariat in Nabanna.” Many other news websites also carried similar visuals in February 2021.#WATCH | West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee nearly falls while driving an electric scooter in Howrah, as a mark of protest against fuel price hike. She quickly regained her balance with support and continued to drive. She is travelling to Kalighat from State Secretariat in Nabanna pic.twitter.com/CnAsQYNhTP — ANI (@ANI) February 25, 2021Further, we did a keyword search, but could not find any recent media report corroborating the viral claim.Thus, it is evident from the above information that an old video of Mamata Banerjee driving an electric scooter is being shared as recent with misleading claims.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Old Video Of Yogi Adityanath Falsely Linked With Nupur... Amid the violence over suspended BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma’s remarks on Prophet Mohammad, a video of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath, has surfaced on social media where he can be seen suggesting ways to deal with communal violence.The above post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above post and found it to be misleading.Upon closely observing the above video, we noticed that UP CM Yogi Adityanath was addressing the Lok Sabha which raised our doubt about the date of video since Yogi Adityanath is no longer a Member of Parliament.We extracted keyframes of the video using InVid software and put them through Reverse Image Search with relevant keywords. The search led us to the full version of the video on the official YouTube channel of the Bharatiya Janata Party dated August 13, 2014, from which the video in question was extracted using different clips.On digging further we found several reports about Yogi Adityanath’s Lok Sabha address dating back to August 13, 2014. These reports can be seen here and here.Yogi Adityanath was earlier a member of Lok Sabha from UP’s Gorakhpur constituency for five successive terms from 1998 to 2017. He gave up his Lok Sabha seat in 2017 when he took over as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh.Hence, with the above findings, it is clear that the video in question is nearly eight year old and has no connection with violence over Nupur Sharma’s remarks.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Old Video Of Bhagwant Mann Dancing Resurfaces As Recent A video of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann is being widely shared on social media in which he can be seen dancing on a jeep. The video is being shared with a claim that Mann celebrated this way after becoming the Chief Minister.The caption reads, “ਮੁੱਖ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਸਾ੍ਹਬ ਜੀ ਏਨਾ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਕਿਹੜੀ ਗੱਲ ਦਾ. ਜੇ ਲੋਕ ਵਿਰੋਧ ਕਰਦੇ ਨੇ ਗੰਦੇ ਇਸ਼ਾਰੇ ਕਿਓ ਕਰਨੇ. ਤੁਸੀ ਹੁਣ ਝੰਡਾ ਅਮਲੀ ਨਹੀ ਤੁਸੀ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਜੇ ਸੰਜਮ ਤੋ ਕੰਮ ਲਵੋ.”(English translation: “Chief Minister, why are you so angry? Why make dirty gestures if people protest You are no longer the flag bearer. If you are the Chief Minister of Punjab, exercise restraint”)The link to the post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile did a fact-check and found the claim to be Misleading.On doing a Google Reverse Image Search with one of the screenshots, we found that the same video was published by Punjabi singer Jassi Jasraj in 2019 with a caption that read, “ਸੌਭਾ ਨੀ ਦਿੰਦੀਆਂ ਇਹ ਗੱਲਾਂ ਭਗਵੰਤ ਮਾਨ ਨੂੰ। ਘਨੌਰ ਕਲਾਂ ਚ ਕੱਲ ਦੀ ਹਰਕਤ ਦੇਖਲੌ ਸਾਮੀ 7 ਵਜੇ ਲੋਕਾ ਨੂੰ ਗਾਲਾਂ ਕੱਡੀਆ ਤੇ ਜਾਦਾ ਹੋਇਆ ਆਪ ਦੇਖੋ ਕਿ ਇਸ਼ਾਰੇ ਕਰ ਗਿਆ……” (English translation: “These things do not give glory to Bhagwant Mann. See tomorrow’s movement in Ghanour Kalan.”)We also found that a Facebook user also shared a news clip from a Punjabi newspaper on May 19, 2019. According to the report, “Bhagwant Mann played DJ in front of Gurudwara Sahib regardless of the time in Ghanauri Kalan village. He also sang, danced to the songs and made obscene gestures toward the villagers.”The report also said that he was then the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Punjab President and Lok Sabha candidate from the Sangrur constituency. He did so in order to stop the ongoing protest by villagers.Bhagwant Mann was sworn in as the Punjab Chief Minister on March 16, 2022, after the party registered a landslide victory in the assembly polls, wresting the state from Congress.Hence, we can conclude that the viral post is misleading.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Old Video From Madhya Pradesh Falsely Linked To Bangladesh... India’s northeastern region and several parts of Bangladesh including Sylhet are seeing the worst flooding in nearly 20 years, which has affected millions of people.In this backdrop, a video showing a temple standing in gushing waters is being widely shared on social media linking it to flooding in Sylhet.The video is being shared on Facebook with a caption in Bengali: “হাজার হাজার ঘর-বাড়ি বাংলাদেশের সিলেট-সুনামগঞ্জে নদীর জলে তলিয়ে যাচ্ছে, কিন্তু ঈশ্বরের ঘর(মন্দির) এখনো মাথা উচু করে দাড়িয়ে আছে.. হর হর মহাদেব”(English translation: Thousands of houses are being submerged in the river in Sylhet-Sunamganj of Bangladesh, But the house of God (temple) is still standing with its head held high)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim and found it to be MISLEADING.A simple Reverse Image Search directed us to a YouTube video uploaded on September 15, 2021, which carried the same viral video stating that it was the Shri Kapileshwar Temple in Sarangpur, Madhya Pradesh.The same visuals were also carried in another YouTube video dated August 22, 2020, with the description, “Sarangpur#MP: Reporter- Shafiq Ansari on river drain overflowing due to heavy rains.”We searched further and found a Vlog on Shri Kapileshwar Temple that carried visuals of the same temple. The temple seen in that vlog is exactly the same as the temple seen in the viral video.We further searched on Google Maps and found that this temple is located in the middle of the Kali Sindh river in Madhya Pradesh.Thus, it is evident from the above information that an old video from Madhya Pradesh is being falsely linked to recent floods in Bangladesh.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Video From Mexico Falsely Shared As Cattle Washed Away... This search directed us to the official YouTube channel “Imagen Noticias”, which carried the same video on July 28, 2020. According to the video description, these were scenes related to the incident of Jakulpan river in Nayarit (Mexico), where cattle were washed away.Taking a cue from this, we searched the web and found a news article published on July 28, 2020, on the same incident.We found the same video uploaded on a Twitter post, dated July 28, 2020, with the caption: “WORLD – Cows are washed away by flood after a high volume of rain caused by the hurricane #Hanna in Compostela, Nayarit, Mexico.”On digging further, we also found the same video on Joranda.com.mx, dated July 28, 2020, claiming that the video is from Hanna, in which thousands of people were affected because of the torrential rains, followed by a storm.Earlier, NewsMobile had also exposed the viral video, which claimed that cattle were washed away in Kerala floods.Thus, the viral video in question is from Hanna, Mexico, having no connection with the recent Bangladesh floods.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: 2020 Image From Turkey Falsely Linked to Afghanistan Earthquake On June 22, a strong earthquake struck a remote, mountainous area of eastern Afghanistan, close to the Pakistani border, killing at least 1,000 people and wounding nearly 1,500.Against this backdrop, an image showing a collapsed building is being widely shared on social media linking it to the recent Afghanistan earthquake.The image is shared on Facebook with a caption in the Arabic language: “زلزال قوي يضرب #أفغانستان , يودي بحياة أكثر من 950 شخصاً ومئات المصابين ودمار هائل في المنازل , حيث ضرب الزلزال مقاطعة باكتيكا شرق البلاد في وقت مبكر من صباح اليوم”(English translation: A powerful earthquake hits #Afghanistan, killing more than 950 people, and injuring thousands with massive destruction of properties, where the earthquake hit Paktika district early this morning)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, and found it to be MISLEADING.Doing a simple Reverse Image Search directed us to Getty Images, which carried the same viral image on January 26, 2020.The image description reads: “Rescue workers at the scene of a collapsed building on January 26, 2020, in Elazig, Turkey. The 6.8-magnitude earthquake injured more than 1,600 people and left some 30 trapped in the wreckage of toppled buildings. Turkey sits on top of two major fault-lines and earthquakes are frequent in the country.”The same image was also featured in a Bloomberg article, dated January 31, 2020, with the description: “Rescue workers at the scene of a collapsed building in Elazig following an earthquake on January 26.”Searching further, we found many news articles published in January 2020 that reported the same earthquake, stating “at least 22 people died and hundreds injured in eastern Turkey after an earthquake rattled the region on Friday evening, according to authorities.”Thus, it is evident from the above information that the viral image is not related to the recent Afghanistan earthquake.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Old Images of Flood-Rescue Operation By Bangladesh Army Reappears... The recent incessant rainfall in Bangladesh’s Sylhet region has claimed at least 25 lives. The devastating flood has also left more than four million people stranded.Against this backdrop, a collage of images is widely shared on social media claiming that it shows Bangladesh Army carrying out a rescue operation in the flood-hit Sylhet region.The image is shared on Facebook with a caption in Bengali language: “আলহামদুলিল্লাহ্‌ উদ্ধারকাজে নিয়োজিত বাংলাদেশের আস্থা বাংলাদেশ সেনাবাহিনী আল্লাহ্‌ এবার আপনি একটু দয়া করুন। সকল আযাব গজব হতে প্রিয় ভূমি বাংলাদেশ ও সিলেট অঞ্চলে পানিবদ্ধ মানুষগুলোকে হিফাজত করুন”(English translation: Alhamdulillah Confidence of Bangladesh engaged in rescue work Bangladesh Army God, now, please. Protect the waterlogged people in the beloved land of Bangladesh and the Sylhet region from all the torment and wrath)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, and found it to be MISLEADING.Doing a simple Reverse Image Search, directed us to a post on the official Facebook page of the Bangladesh Army, dated June 19, 2018, which published the same images. The caption reads: “Bangladesh Army next to the flood victims in Moulvibazar”.The same image had been carried by a Facebook page — ‘Bangla Fact’, on June 20, 2018, with a caption: “Ignoring the Eid vacation, Bangladesh Army besides the flood victims of Moulvibazar. Thank you”Taking a cue from this, we did a keyword search and found a news report published by a Bangladesh news website on June 16, 2018, reporting that “the flood situation in Moulvibazar has further deteriorated due to the downpour from upper reaches.” In June 2018, when the flood situation deteriorated in Moulvibazar, the Bangladesh Army was involved in the overall relief and rescue work of the flood victims.Thus, it is clear that an old set of images is being falsely shared as recent visuals of the Bangladesh Army carrying out a rescue operation in the flood-hit Sylhet region.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: No This Video Does NOT Vandalism At Bihar Deputy... Protests over the Agnipath recruitment scheme escalated in Bihar on June 17, when a mob attacked Deputy Chief Minister Renu Devi’s house, damaged railway properties, and disrupted normal life in many districts.Against this backdrop, a video is being widely shared on social media with the people standing under a white two-story house and smashing things, claiming that angry mobs vandalising Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Renu Devi’s house.The video is shared on Facebook with a caption in the Bengali: “এটা কিন্তু বিহারের উপ মুখ্যমন্ত্রীর বাড়ি শ্রীলঙ্কা পার্ট ২” (English translation: This is Bihar’s Deputy Chief Minister’s house. Sri Lanka part 2)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, and found it to be MISLEADING.Doing a keyword search, we found a news report published by Hindustan Times that Bihar Deputy Chief Minister’s house was vandalised by Agnipath protesters. It also embedded a video tweeted by ANI. Although in this video, the house is not clearly visible, one can see a blue structured building being vandalised and not white.#WATCH | Bihar: The residence of Deputy CM Renu Devi, in Bettiah, attacked by agitators during their protest against #AgnipathScheme Her son tells ANI, “Our residence in Bettiah was attacked. We suffered a lot of damage. She (Renu Devi) is in Patna.” pic.twitter.com/Ow5vhQI5NQ — ANI (@ANI) June 17, 2022Searching further, we found a clearer version of vandalism at Renu Devi’s home in Bihar, uploaded by Times Now on June 17, 2022. This video also shows a different house being attacked.We then extracted keyframes from the viral video using the InVid Tool and performed a Reverse Image Search. This search directed us to a tweet upload on June 17, that carried the same viral video. The text reads: “Protesting students reached BJP office in Bagaha. BJP office vandalised, papers blown in the wind.”We also found the same video uploaded by Alok Kumar, Editor of The Times of India’s Hindi edition. It also stated: “The BJP on the receiving end of #Agnipath protesters as its three MLAs and house of the Deputy CM in #Bihar were attacked in the last 24 hours. Protesters are now attacking its offices. This video is of the Bagha BJP office.”The BJP on the receiving end of #Agnipath protestors as its Three MLAs and house of the deputy CM in #Bihar were attacked in the last 24 hours. Protestors are now attacking its offices. This video is of Bagha BJP office#AgnipathRecruitmentScheme #AgnipathScheme pic.twitter.com/0P7XMEMXLV — Alok Kumar (@dmalok) June 17, 2022Many newspapers and media channels have also reported about BJP’s Bihar office being vandalised over Agnipath protests.Thus, it is confirmed that the video on BJP’s Bihar office incident is being falsely shared as Bihar Deputy Cheif Minister’s house. Therefore, the viral claim is misleading.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Video Of Protest Against ‘Agnipath’ Scheme In Bihar Linked... Amidst the ongoing nationwide protests over the contentious ‘Agnipath’ scheme, video of a burning train is being shared online, claiming that the visuals are from Secunderabad in Telangana.The video is being shared with a caption, “तेलंगाना के सिकंदराबाद में अग्निपथ स्कीम के विरोध में हुई आगजनी की घटना”(English Translation: Arson incident in Telangana’s Secunderabad against Agnipath scheme)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the post and found it to be misleading.We ran a keyword search along with a Reverse Image Search on the keyframes of the video and found that the same video was featured in an NDTV report dated June 17, 2022. As per the report, the video is from Lakhisarai, Bihar.Mojo Story also uploaded the same video on YouTube on June 17, 2022, with the title, “Agnipath | Trains Set On Fire In Bihar On 3rd Day Of Protest | Over 34 Trains Cancelled By Railways.”This proves that the video is from Bihar and not Telangana.However, we did find reports of Secunderabad Railway Station being vandalised and that of a train being set ablaze by agitators in Telangana.#WATCH | Telangana: Secunderabad railway station vandalised and a train set ablaze by agitators who are protesting against #AgnipathRecruitmentScheme. pic.twitter.com/2llzyfT4XG — ANI (@ANI) June 17, 2022Hence, from the above information, it is clear that the post in circulation is misleading.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Did 34 Nations Extend Support To Suspended BJP Leader... Amid ongoing protests in India and abroad over suspended BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma’s controversial statement on Prophet Mohammad, a claim is doing rounds on social media suggesting that 34 nations including Russia, Netherlands, France and Israel have extended their support to Sharma.The claim in Hindi reads: “रूस नीदरलैंड फ्रांस इजरायल सहित कुल 34 देशों ने नुपुर शर्मा और भारत का समर्थन किया।।। जय श्री राम”(English Translation: “A total of 34 countries including Russia, Netherlands, France, Israel have supported Nupur Sharma and India. Long live Ram”The above post can be seen here.The same tweet was also attributed to Major General (Retd) GB Bakshi.The tweet can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim and found it to be false as we could not find any official statement by any country supporting Nupur Sharma.Upon running a relevant Google search we did not find any news report corroborating the viral claim that 34 countries have supported the suspended BJP leader.However, Dutch politician, Geert Wilders (member of the opposition), did Tweet in support of Sharma, but the Netherlands did not release any official statement on the matter.It is ridiculous that Arab and Islamic countries are angered by Indian politician #NupurSharma @NupurSharmaBJP for speaking the truth about #ProphetMuhammad who indeed married Aisha when she was six years old and consumed the marriage when she was nine. Why does India apologize? — Geert Wilders (@geertwilderspvv) June 6, 2022Hence, we can conclude that the claim of 34 nations supporting Nupur Sharma is False.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Letter Claiming ‘ORs Attested After Jan 2019 Will Come... A letter attributed to the Ministry of Defence is being circulated on social media claiming personnel under ‘Other Ranks (ORs) attested after 01 January 2019 and not promoted to the substantive rank of Naik or equivalent on 01 July 2022 are to be kept under the new Agnipath Scheme’.Facebook users are sharing the letter with text, “मोदी सरकार का एक और #दमनकारी_फैसला। भारतीय सेना में जो जवान 31 December 2018 के बाद भर्ती हुए हैं वो सभी जवान “अग्निवीर” घोषित कर दिये हैं।”(English Translation: Another #oppressive_decision of Modi government. All the soldiers who have joined the Indian Army after 31 December 2018 have been declared “Agniveer”.)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the post and found it to be false.We ran a keyword search but did not any credible media report to corroborate the claim. Under the Agnipath scheme, around 46,000 soldiers will be recruited between the ages of 17-and-a -half years and 21 years (23 for the year 2022) into the three armed services on a four-year short-term contractual basis.Moreover, in the letter, the date mentioned is June 17, 2022. However, we scanned through the press note on the website of the Ministry of Defence but did not any such letter.On searching further, we also found that Press Information Bureau had also refuted the claim in a tweet dated June 20, 2022.Hence, from the above fact check, it is clear that the viral letter is fake.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Old Newspaper Clipping About Death Of Army Aspirant Linked... A picture of a newspaper clipping about the death of an army aspirant is being shared on social media. The posts are linking the clipping with the new ‘Agnipath’ scheme announced by the Centre for recruitment of youngsters in the Defence forces.The Facebook post reads, “ARMY की तैयारी करने वाले सभी भाइयों से निवेदन है कि कोई भी गलत कदम नहीं उठाए, क्योंकि आपलोग का जीवन आपके परिवार के लिए आर्मी से बढ़कर है, क्योंकि एक माँ अपने बेटा को बेरोजगार देख कर जी सकती है, लेकिन खो कर नहीं जी सकती है.”(English Translation: All the brothers preparing for ARMY are requested not to take any wrong step, because your life is greater than the army for your family, because a mother can live by seeing her son unemployed, but cannot live by losing him.)The headline of the report read, “बापू! इस जन्म में फौजी नहीं बन पाया, अगले जन्म में ज़रूर बनूँगा” (English: Father! I could not become a soldier in this life, I will definitely become one in the next life.)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the post and found that the newspaper clipping is old.We ran a keyword search and multiple reports with the same headline which were published on April 29, 2022, a few months before the ‘Agnipath’ scheme was announced in June.According to reports, a resident of Bhiwani, Haryana ended his life as he failed to clear the army test even after several attempts. The reports identified him as Pavan, who was 23 years old.A report by Indian Express stated that the 23-year-old army aspirant allegedly died by suicide at a village in Bhiwani district after turning ‘overage’ for recruitment.The report also mentioned that Pavan cleared the physical fitness exam for Army recruitment two or three times but could not make it to the final cut-off. And he crossed the age bar during the pandemic when the recruitment process was put on hold.Hence, based on the above information, it is clear that the newspaper clipping is not related to ‘Agnipath’ scheme.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old Video Of Protests Falsely Linked To ‘Agnipath’ Row Following the announcement of the ‘Agnipath’ scheme by the Centre on June 14, there have been massive protests in several states across the country.Against this backdrop, a video in which a protester can be seen urging the government to roll back the scheme is being widely shared on social media.The video is being shared on Facebook with a Hindi caption, “जब “अग्निपथ” पर चलने “अग्निवीरों” की बात आती है तो जेहन में सबसे पहले ऐसे “अग्निवीर” ही क्यों आ जाते हैं”(English translation: When it comes to “firefighters” walking on “fire” Why do such “Agnivir” come first in Jehan)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim and found it to be MISLEADING.Upon carefully watching the video, we noticed the logo of ‘Principle of News’ in the top right corner. Taking a cue from this, we did a keyword search on YouTube and found the same video was uploaded on a channel named ‘Principle of News’ on January 28, 2022.The video description reads, “I don’t know the meaning of RRB-NTPC but protest for the students doing it”. In this video, some journalists are seen questioning a person who describes himself as a supporter of Lalu Yadav and RJD.Searching further, we found that in January 2022, there was a huge uproar in Patna with regards to the Railway-NTPC examination.Though we could not ascertain the exact location and time of the viral video, it is evident from the above information that the video has been on the internet at least since January 2022 and is not related to the recent ‘Agnipath’ protests.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Pictures of Naga Sadhus Falsely Linked With Support For... Social media users are sharing images of Naga Sadhus carrying swords. The images claim that they are protesting in support of former BJP spokesperson, Nupur Sharma, who sparked the controversy over remarks on Prophet Mohammad.The image is shared with a caption: “नागा साधुओं ने भी #नुपुरशर्मा के समर्थन का ऐलान कर दिया हैं कल्पना करिये उस दृष्य ” का जब “18 लाख” नागा साधु सड़क पर उतरेंगे। महा तांडव आपका स्वागत है,हर हर महादेव” (English translation: “Naga sadhus have also announced their support for #NupurSharma… imagine the scene when “18 lakh” Naga sadhus will hit the road. Welcome to Maha Tandav, Har Har Mahadev.”)The link to the post can be seen here.FACT CHECKWhen NewsMobile fact-checked the claim, it was found to be fake.Image 1:On doing a Google Reverse Image Search, we found the same image uploaded by a website Yatradha.com, dated May 13, 2020. The image claimed that it was of Kumbh Mela.Image 2:We also found the same image uploaded by the NewsLive.com website on April 12, 2021. The article associated with the image claimed that it was of believers who came to take a dip in Ganga during Kumbh Mela in Haridwar.Image 3:We found the same image was also uploaded by India TV, dated July 3, 2014, with a caption: “Naga sadhus asked to gather to confront Sai Baba followers.”Image 4:Another website — Abhishekhajela — had also uploaded the same image with a caption claiming that it was of Kumbh Mela.Hence, we can ascertain that the viral claim is fake.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: The Image Of Protesters Burning Indian Flag Is NOT... An image of a few people burning the Indian flag is being circulated on social media with a claim that it shows a protest in India over controversial remarks on the Prophet by Nupur Sharma.Facebook users shared the image with the caption: “Peaceful Muslims burning our Tiranga (National Flag) today in India. #HindusUnderAttackInIndia”Here’s the link to the post.FACT CHECKWhen NewsMobile fact-checked the post, it was found to be misleading.We put the image through Reverse Image Search and found the same image in a report by ABC News. As per the report, the image is of a recent protest in Pakistan.The same image was published by Al Jazeera, dated June 10, 2022, with the caption: “Protesters burning the Indian flag during a demonstration — to condemn the derogatory remarks by BJP members against Islam and Prophet Muhammad — in Lahore [K M Chaudary/AP]”The same was also published by The Washington Post, dated June 9, 2022. We also found the original image on the Associated Press website, with the caption: “Supporters of religious groups burn a representation of Indian flag during a demonstration to condemn derogatory references to Islam and the Prophet Muhammad recently made by Nupur Sharma, a spokesperson of the governing Indian Hindu nationalist party, in Lahore, Pakistan, Thursday, June 9, 2022. (AP Photo/K.M. Chaudary)”Hence, it is certain that the image is from Pakistan, NOT India, as being claimed in the viral post.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: This Post About Railway Concessions For Senior Citizens Is... Many social media users are sharing a post, claiming that Indian Railways has resumed concession for senior citizens. According to the post, males above 60 years of age will be given a relaxation of 40% and women will get 50% on railway fares.The post reads: “Railway concession will resume w.e.f 1.7.2022. Male/60 years: 40%,Female/58 years: 50%.”The link to the post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile did the fact-check, and found it to be fake.On searching with appropriate keywords, we found a report published by India.com on May 24, 2022. According to the report, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had said that Indian Railways lifted concessions on ticket prices provided to senior citizens. The decision was taken as the Railways was already giving subsidy on train tickets. He stated that people were only charged ₹45 per ticket and the government had to pay ₹100 per ticket for operational costs. And the concession was suspended only for two years due to the Covid-19 pandemic.We also found that PIB Fact Check had refuted the viral claim, tweeting: “A #Fake media report is claiming that Indian Railways will resume concessions for senior citizens from July 1, 2022. No such announcement has been made by @RailMinIndia. Indian Railways is currently providing concessions only to divyangjans, patients and students.”Hence. we can ascertain that the viral claim is fake.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Video of Khalistani Supporters Disrupting Rahul Gandhi’s London Event... A video is going viral on social media platforms showing some people raising pro-Congress, pro-Khalistan and anti-India slogans, while a Congress poster can be seen on a wall. Many social media users have shared this video with the claim that Khalistan supporters reached Rahul Gandhi’s event in London to support Congress party.A Facebook user shared the video with the caption in Hindi that translates to: “How can I hand over my country to Congress, you tell… Khalistani terrorists reached Rahul Gandhi’s meeting in London… Raised slogans of Congress Party zindabad and Hindustan murdabad… Send to all the groups you have.”(Original: कैसे सौंप दु मै काँग्रेस को अपना देश,आप ही बताओ… लंदन मे राहुल गांधी की सभा मे पहुचे खलीस्थानी आतकंवादी… काँग्रेस पार्टी जिंदाबाद और हिंदुस्थान मुर्दाबाद नारे लगाये…आपके पास जितने भी ग्रुप है सब मे भेजो)FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the viral video, and found it to be shared with a false claim.On performing keyword searches, we found a report published on the Indian Express website on August 26, 2018. The headline of the article reads: “Khalistan supporters attempt to disrupt Rahul Gandhi’s event in London”As per the report, three pro-Khalistan supporters tried to disrupt his public event on August 26, 2018. It stated that the activists managed to enter the event where Gandhi was to deliver the inaugural address at the Indian Overseas Congress UK Mega Conference, and started shouting “Khalistan zindabad”. The audience then began to counter-chant “Congress party zindabad” in reaction to the attempted disruption. The Khalistan supports were later ushered outside by Scotland Yard officers following a minor scuffle.“The protesters — three men and a woman — were escorted out of the hotel by the police on Saturday night. They later told TOI that it was a protest against Gandhi’s Friday’s remarks on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. According to the report, the incident was seen as a major security breach.”We also found the same news uploaded on WION YouTube channel, on August 27, 2018.Therefore, it can be concluded that the video is being shared with a false claim.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old Video Clip Falsely Shared As Angry Mobs Surrounding... A video is being widely shared on social media, claiming that angry mobs have surrounded suspended BJP leader Nupur Sharma’s house for her controversial comments against the Prophet that led to international backlash.The video is shared on Facebook with a caption in the Bengali language: “নুপুর শর্মার বাড়ি ঘেরাও করেছে জনতা” (English translation: People surrounded Nupur Sharma’s house)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, and found it to be FALSE.Using the InVid Tool, we extracted keyframes from the viral video and performed a Reverse Image Search. This search directed us to the YouTube channel of OTV, which carried the same viral video on January 6, 2022. The video description reads: “BJP workers and police clash outside the Bhadrak Collector office”Taking a cue from this, we searched further and found the video uploaded by News 18 Odia on January 6, 2022, reporting the same incident. Odisha TV also reported the incident in January 2022.We also found a tweet — dated January 6, 2022 — by OTV that carried a screengrab from the viral video. The text reads: “#BJP workers scuffle with police while barging into the office of Bhadrak Collector during their protest over the alleged neglect of the state government in implementing OBC reservation #Odisha.”#BJP workers scuffle with police while barging into the office of Bhadrak Collector during their protest over alleged neglect of state govt in implementation of OBC reservation #Odisha pic.twitter.com/RYgw11CpzW — OTV (@otvnews) January 6, 2022Thus, it is now clear that an old and unrelated video from Odisha is being falsely shared as an angry mob surrounded Nupur Sharma’s house, and the viral claim is false.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Does The Viral Video Show Cop Murdered By Rioters... After former BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma’s controversial remarks on Prophet Muhammad, protests have erupted across the country. In the above context, a video is being widely shared on social media in which a crowd can be seen in front of a dead cop. The caption associated with the video says that rioters killed him in West Bengal.The video is shared with a caption that reads, “कोलकाता में दंगाइयों ने पुलिस वाले को मार डाला, उसके बाद उसके साथी को भी धमकी दे रहे है.” (English translation, “In Kolkata, rioters killed the policeman, after that, they also threatened his partner.”)The link to the post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile did a fact-check and found the claim to be false.On searching with appropriate keywords, we found a YouTube video published by NDTV on June 10, 2022. The description associated with the video read, “A police constable posted at the Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata fired multiple rounds before shooting himself dead today. A woman who was hit in the firing reportedly died.”The report was also published by Indian Express. According to the report, “A police constable in his late 20s, posted at the office of the deputy high commissioner, opened fire indiscriminately from his rifle on Friday afternoon killing a woman riding pillion. Later, he died by suicide by shooting himself. What prompted the policeman identified as Chodup Lepcha to open fire is yet to be ascertained.”Hence, we can ascertain that the viral claim is false.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Did Amit Shah Write To Uttarakhand CM To Provide... After BJP suspended Nupur Sharma for controversial remarks on the Prophet, which triggered massive communal clashes in many parts of the nation, a letter purportedly written by Home Minister Amit Shah is widely being shared on social media. According to the letter, Shah has asked Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Dhami to provide Z-class security to Nupur Sharma.The letter in circulation reads, “Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami, I admire your efforts to maintain Law & Order in the state and your keen interest to provide Z security to Shri Ajay Gupta is also commendable. In current scenario, I recommend you to critically evaluate emerging threats to the family house of Smt Nupur Sharma in Dehradun and provide Z security on urgent basis. I am confident that you will manage well and efficiently execute this task. Both Shri Ajay Gupta and Smt Nupur Sharma are icons to promote Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ideology that will ultimately lead us to accomplish Hindu Rashtra goal. I hope, you will understand the sensitive nature of this task and give your prime importance. My best wishes to you and your team.. Yours sincerely, Amit Shah.”The link to the post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile did a fact-check and found the claim to be fake.On searching with appropriate keywords, we could not find any media report about Amit Shah writing to Pushkar Dhami regarding Nupur Sharma’s security.We also found that a similar letter that went viral in 2021 which had the same H.M.P. number as the one viral now and had the same fold mark on the bottom right corner of the page. NewsMobile had then done a fact-check that can be seen here.PIB Fact Check also refuted the claim. The tweet read, “A letter is doing rounds on social media claiming to be written by Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, to CM of Uttarakhand, Pushkar Singh Dhami.”Thus we can ascertain that the viral letter is fake.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Does This Video Show Youth Protesting Against Agnipath scheme?... A video has surfaced on social media platforms showing a huge crowd with a claim that the video shows a crowd protesting the new ‘Tour of Duty’ (ToD) or Agnipath scheme.Under the scheme, around 46,000 soldiers will be recruited between the ages of 17-and-a -half years and 21 years (23 for the year 2022) into the three armed services on a four-year short-term contractual basis.Some Facebook are sharing the post with the caption, “#किसानों ने काले कानून वापस करा दिए थे युवा #अग्निवीर की योजना को वापस करायेगा”(English Translation: The farmers managed to get the black farm laws rolled back, the Youth will get #Agniveer to roll back too)The posts can be seen here and here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the video and found that it had been shared with a false claim.With the help of a Reverse Image Search using the keyframes, we found the same video uploaded on a YouTube channel on January 4, 2021, with the caption, “Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi Chehlum | TLP Chehlum 2021.” As per the YouTube video, the visuals are from Lahore, Pakistan.On checking further with relevant keywords, we found that the chief of Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP), Khadim Hussain Rizvi passed away on November 19, 2020. His Chehlum, which is a religious observance in Islam held 40 days after the death of a person, was observed on January 3, 2021, near Mosque Rehmatul Lil Alameen at Multan Road’s Battery Stop in Lahore. It was attended by thousands of people in Pakistan, which can be seen in the viral video.NewsMobile debunked the same video in November 2021, which was shared as a protest in Mumbai against Tripura violence. The same video was recently shared as a protest against Nupur Sharma’s remarks on the Prophet and the crowd chanting Hanuman Chalisa in Jaipur.https://newsmobile.in/articles/2022/06/16/fact-check-old-video-from-pak-falsely-shared-as-people-chanting-hanuman-chalisa-in-jaipur/Thus it is clear that the viral video is old and is NOT from India. Hence, it can be concluded that the video is being shared with a false claim.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: No, This Image Does Not Show Nupur Sharma Visiting... content: Fact Check: Viral Video of People Driving Over Indian Flag Is... A video — showing a bunch of people driving over the Indian national flag and waving a Pakistan flag — is being widely shared on social media, claiming that these are the visuals from Tamil Nadu.The video is shared on Facebook with a Hindi caption: “इस विडियो को देखें और इसे जितना हो सके उतना फॉरवर्ड करें …. अगर आप यू आज चुप रहते हैं तो हमें नुकसान होगा … क्योंकि 6 महीने के बाद इसे आगे बढ़ाने का कोई फायदा नहीं होगा … उँगलियाँ घुमाएँ और इसे आगे बढ़ाएँ अभी – तांजोर, तमिलनाडु” (English translation: Watch this video and forward it as much as possible… If you remain silent today, we will lose… Because after six months it won’t be worth pushing… Fingers crossed and forward it now – Tanjore, Tamil Nadu)Here’s the link to the above post.The video is being widely shared on Facebook with similar claims.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim and found it to be MISLEADING.As stated earlier, numerous people can be seen holding the Pakistani flag in the viral video. We saw a white vehicle with the words “The Hunar Foundation” printed on it about three minutes and 38 seconds into the video.The Hunar Foundation is a Karachi-based organisation that focuses on delivering technical training in Pakistan, according to its website.At the beginning of the video, we spotted a store sign with the word “Sanam” written on it. When we looked for Sanam businesses in Karachi, we found a “Sanam Boutique” with the same typeface and style as the one in the video. The store, according to this website, is located on Karachi’s Tariq Road.We identified the Sanam Boutique featuring in a YouTube video of Tariq Road in Karachi in 2017.Searching further, we found that identical videos and screengrabs from it have been circulating on the Internet since March 2020.Though we were not able to ascertain the exact time and location of the viral video, it is evident from the above information that the viral video is old and not from Tamil Nadu but from Karachi, Pakistan.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Qatar Airways CEO’s Spoof Interview Goes Viral As Real In the backdrop of Qatar condemning the derogatory remarks against the Prophet by a BJP spokesperson, a video has surfaced on the Internet, showing Qatar Airways CEO Akbar Al Baker. In the video, he is reacting to the plea made by a Twitter user ‘Vashudev’, who had called for a boycott of Qatar Airways.After as many as 15 Islamic nations, including Qatar, condemned the remarks by former BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma against the Prophet, many special media users called for a boycott of Qatar Airways.One such user was Vashudev who posted a video on June 6, 2022, in which he appealed to boycott Qatar Airways. But an Al Jazeera interview clip of Qatar Airways CEO Akbar Al Baker, meantime, has gone viral, in which he could be seen reacting to Vashudev.In the video, Al Baker can be heard saying that Vashudev is the biggest shareholder in Qatar Airways… and after he threatened to boycott the airline, he (Al Baker) rushed back to Qatar.The post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the viral clip, and found it to be doctored.First, on a keyword search, we did not find any statement from Qatar Airways or its CEO on the boycott.We then extracted keyframes of the video and put them through the Reverse Image Search with keywords such as ‘Qatar Airways’, ‘CEO, ‘Akbar Al Baker’, and ‘Al Jazeera’. And we found the original Al Baker interview on the official YouTube channel of Al Jazeera English was dated June 13, 2017.The interview was taken by e-interview with Al Jazeera journalist Andrew Simmons about the finances of the global airline.Now, it can be noticed that the clip from the original interview (0:47 seconds to 3:46 minutes) was extracted and a voice-over was superimposed, using video editing software.In the original video, the CEO spoke about the airspace ban by some of its neighbouring countries, when they accused Qatar of supporting “terrorism”.So, it can be concluded that the viral video in question is a spoof of Qatar Airways CEO’s interview from 2017.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Satirical Article Viral as Canada Banning Straight Marriages During... During the ongoing pride month celebrations across various countries in the month of June, a screengrab of a 2019 news article, headlined ‘Canada to ban straight marriage during pride month’, is making the rounds on social media. It further states: “Justin Trudeau announced the month-long straight marriage ban yesterday in Halifax to a teary-eyed gathering.”There’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, and found it to be FALSE.We noticed NPC Daily written at the top of the article. Taking a cue from this, we performed a keyword search and this led us to the website “NPCDaily”. On further scanning the website, we found a section which states: “NPC Daily is a satire site, providing political and cultural commentary with wanton sarcasm. NPC Daily pokes fun of modern journalism and liberalism.”The FAQ section of the website has clearly stated: “NPC Daily is not a legitimate or real news site. However, it is a legitimate source of good laugh.”We also found the viral article ‘Canada to ban straight marriage during pride month’, dated June 10, 2019. The article was published by Quinn Barton and has probably gone viral now owing to the pride month celebrations in the entire world.Quinn Barton, according to her profile on the website, is a social activist and member of an anti-fascism and anti-racism movement that goes by the name of Boston Antifa. Her profile further stresses the fact that “This entire site is satire.”We further checked the social media handles of NPC Daily. Their Instagram bio reads ‘Your source for News and Political Commentary. Trusted non-biased liberal news source – satire’ and their Facebook page is categorised under Satire/Parody. Their Twitter bio reads: “Official site for NPC Daily. News and Political Commentary. (Parody site — nothing on this site or page is meant to be taken seriously)”.There was no official statement or news by any Canadian authorities that stated the banning of straight marriages in the country during pride month.Thus, it is crystal clear that the screenshot of a satirical article is being falsely shared as Canada bans straight marriage during the pride month.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Old Video From Pak Falsely Shared As Recent Protest... All for of ‘La ilaha illallahu muhammadur rasulullah’ #OurProphetOurHonour)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the video and found that it had been shared with a false claim.With the help of Reverse Image Search using the keyframes, we found the same video uploaded on a YouTube channel on January 4, 2021, with the caption, “Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi Chehlum | TLP Chehlum 2021.” As per the YouTube video, the visuals are from Lahore, Pakistan.On checking further with relevant keywords, we found that the chief of Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP), Khadim Hussain Rizvi passed away on November 19, 2020. content: Fact Check: Man Involved In Water Slide Mishap Did Not Die;... A video of a waterslide mishap has surfaced on the internet in which a man in a pool collided with another individual who came down the slide. The man can further be seen bleeding. It has been claimed that the incident took place at Blue World in Uttar Pradesh’s Kanpur and the man was killed in the incident.The video was shared on the Facebook page TV9 Uttar Pradesh and the caption in Hindi read: “कानपुर के ‘ब्लू वर्ड’ में वॉटर एरिया में युवक की मौत। स्लाइडर से नीचे आते समय दूसरे युवक से टकराया, वॉटर पार्क में युवक की मौत का वीडियो हो रहा वायरलबिठूर थाना क्षेत्र के ब्लू वर्ड का बताया जा रहा है वायरल वीडियो।”(English Translation: Youth dies in water area in ‘Blue Word’ in Kanpur. While coming down from the slider, he collided with another young man, the video of the death of the young man in the water park is being viral. The viral video is being told of the blue word of the Bithur police station area)The post can be seen hereFACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim and found it to be false.We extracted keyframes of the video and put them through Reverse Image Search. The result led us to a Dainik Bhaskar report dated June 4, 2022, which featured the same video. According to Dainik Bhaskar’s report, the incident took place at Mukundra Water Park in Rajasthan’s Jhalawar. The man’s life was saved after he was rushed to SRG hospital.Several other reports of the incident can be seen here and here.We further scanned through pictures of Mukundra Water Park on Google maps and established that the video in question is from Jhalawar.Hence, it can be concluded that the video in question is from Rajasthan NOT Kanpur and the man did not die as claimed in the above post.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Old Video From Maharashtra Falsely Linked to Recent Kanpur... On June 3, 2022, Kanpur (UP) witnessed heavy stone-pelting after a clash broke out between two groups over a BJP spokesperson’s allegedly insulting remarks about Prophet Mohammad. According to reports, 36 individuals have been detained and more than 1,000 are being held on suspicion of rioting.Against this backdrop, a video is being widely shared on social media, claiming that Kanpur police are taking action against the rioters on the street at night.The video is shared on Facebook with a Hindi caption: “आधी रात को कानपुर की गलियों से आती हुई उह, आह की आवाज़ को ही शास्त्रों में शुकुन कहा गया है UP पुलिस का कानपुर दंगाइयों पर कहर” (English translation: The sound of Uh.. Ah coming from the streets of Kanpur at midnight is called Shukun in the scriptures. UP police wreaking havoc on Kanpur rioters)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, and found it to be MISLEADING.Using the InVid Tool, we extracted keyframes from the viral video and performed a Reverse Image Search. This search directed us to several social media posts uploaded in April 2020 that carried the same viral video claiming that the video is from Indore and Telangana. This clearly means that the viral video is old and not related to recent Kanpur violence.Taking a cue from this, we conducted a keyword search in Hindi and discovered many news items published on Hindi news portals that detailed the true narrative behind the video. According to these news reports, the Video of police ‘lathi-charge’ is from the Sri Lanka Mumbra area of Thane, Maharashtra.According to a video news report, published by a Hindi news channel, the incident happened when followers of two local politicians clashed on March 27, 2020 in Sri Lanka area of Mumbra, Maharashtra. To disperse the throng and regain control of the situation, the police used batons on the protesters.Thus, it is evident from the above information that an old video from Maharashtra is being falsely linked to recent violence in Kanpur.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Old Video Falsely Linked to ‘Welcome Event’ of Hardik... Gujarat Patidar leader Hardik Patel joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on June 2, days after leaving the Congress. Against this backdrop, a video is being widely shared on social media, claiming that he was welcomed by BJP with a ‘slap’.The video is shared on Facebook with a Hindi caption: “भाजपा में शामिल होते ही हार्दिक पटेल का जोरदार स्वागत एवं अभिनंदन” (English translation: Hardik Patel’s warm welcome and congratulations as soon as he joined BJP)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, and found it to be MISLEADING.Doing a simple keyword search directed us to several news articles that reported the same incident in 2019. An article published by The Economic Times, on April 19, 2019, carried similar visuals stating that “Congress leader Hardik Patel was slapped by an unidentified man while addressing a poll rally on Friday at a village in Surendranagar district, Gujarat.”We found a video news report published by Hindustan Times that carried the same viral video on April 19, 2019. The descriptor reads: “Congress leader Hardik Patel was slapped during a rally in Surendranagar district, Gujarat . While Hardik was addressing the audience, a man charged into the stage and slapped him.”A report by India Today further stated that Tarun Gajjar was eventually recognised as the individual who slapped Patel. Gajjar hit the Patidar leader because he had a personal grievance against him, according to the report.Thus, it is evident from the above information that an old video is being falsely linked to Hardik Patel joining BJP. Therefore, the viral claim is misleading.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Video Game Clip Falsely Linked to Russia-Ukraine Conflict A video has surfaced on the Internet with a missile man striking down a helicopter, claiming that a Russian helicopter has been struck down.The 3:28-minute video further shows combat with forces. The caption reads: “Russi helicopter gunship shot down in flames”The post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above post, and found it to be misleading.We extracted the keyframes of the video and put them through Google Reverse Image Search. The search led us to several gameplay videos /gaming streams of Arma 3.We further scanned through the official website of Arma 3, where we found several visuals of the game similar to the video in question.Based on the description, we ran a keyword search and found that ARMA 3 is an open-world, realism-based, military tactical shooter video game, developed and published by Bohemia Interactive.NewsMobile has debunked similar posts earlier. The article can be seen here, here and here.https://newsmobile.in/articles/2022/05/31/fact-check-game-video-goes-viral-as-russian-copter-being-shot-down/https://newsmobile.in/articles/2022/05/26/fact-check-visuals-from-video-game-falsely-shared-as-drone-attack-on-russian-airfield/Hence, we can conclude that the video in question is a clip from a video game and has no connection with the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: This Picture Does Not Show Temple Turned into Mosque... Many social media users are sharing an image of a religious structure with a dome that looks like a temple. The image is shared with a claim that it is of a mosque, which was built on the base of a Hindu temple.The image is shared with a caption: “Stunningly beautiful walls | with an ugly-looking dome | Chittor temple converted into a mosque by Mughals… ”The link to the post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile did a fact-check, and found the claim to be fake.On doing a Google Reverse Image, we found the same image was published by Shuttercock with a caption: “Shani Deity Temple at Chittor Fort in Chittorgarh city, Rajasthan, India.”We found the picture of the front entrance of the temple, which was published by 123rf.com with a caption: “Shani Deity Altar, Chittorgarh, Rajasthan, India.”Another website Thinking Particle described the temple as “inscription of the pillar near western door of the temple mentions that Velaka, son of Kola — treasurer of Maharana Kumbha, built this temple and dedicated it to Shree Santinatha in 1448, and that it was consecrated by Jina Sagara Suri. The temple, which was later covered by the massive wall built by Banbir, is now kept open.”Hence, we can ascertain that the viral image is of a temple, and a mosque has not been constructed on it.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: 2014 Video of ‘Man Swimming On Road In Kerala’... A video of a man swimming on a waterlogged road is being circulated on social media with a claim that it was shot recently in Kerala.The video was shared with the Malayalam caption: “ടൂറിസവും ഗതാഗതവും ഒരു കുടക്കീഴിൽ നമ്പർവൺ കേരളത്തിൽ” (English translation: Tourism and transportation under one umbrella is number one in Kerala)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the post, and found it to be old.We extracted the keyframes of the video and put them through Reverse Image Search along with some keywords. We found that the same video was shared on YouTube in August 2014 with the title: “funny man swimming on the road, Kerala.”We also found multiple reports from 2014, mentioning that a tourist jumped in to take a swim in the waterlogged street in Kerala. A report by Scroll identified the man as Noam Offray.The same was reported by India Today and Malayalam Oneindia.Hence, from the above fact check, it is clear that the video is an old one.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Old Video Falsely Shared As Protest Rally By Former... Imran Khan was ousted as Prime Minister of Pakistan on April 10, 2022, following a vote of no confidence in the National Assembly. Khan had held protest rallies around the country since then, attracting audiences in the tens of thousands. According to media reports, Imran Khan’s political party held an ‘Azadi March’ in Islamabad on May 26, which led to the deployment of the Pakistan Army in the capital city and tear gas shelling.Against this backdrop, a video is being widely shared on social media, claiming that it shows visuals of the ‘worst tear gas shelling’ in Islamabad after the ‘Azadi March’.The video is shared on Facebook with a caption in the Urdu language: “اسلام آباد میں صبح کا آغاز اور بد ترین آنسو گیس کی شیلنگ۔” (English translation: Morning starts in Islamabad and worst tear gas shelling)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, and found it to be MISLEADING.Putting the keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the results directed us to a tweet, dated February 10, 2021, that carried the same viral video reading: “#Islamabad D Chowk right now #EmployeesProtest.” This clearly means that the video is old and not related to recent protests in Islamabad.The same video was also uploaded by another Twitter user on February 10, 2021, with the caption: “A few years ago, when Imran Khan’s party attacked PTV & Parliament in Islamabad, the protesters were not treated like that. Adopting democratic traditions is not easy for everyone.”Taking a cue from this, we did a keyword search and found the same video uploaded on the official Instagram page of Dawn Today on February 10, 2021, with the caption: “Clouds of smoke are seen as Islamabad police resort to tear gas shelling amid an ongoing protest by government employees for a pay raise in the capital.”View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dawn Today (@dawn.today)Gulf Today also carried the same viral visuals on February 11, 2021, with the text: “Islamabad police fire tear gas shells to disperse protesting government employees demanding pay raise.”Thus, it is evident from the above information that an old video of government employees’ protests is being falsely linked to recent unrest in Islamabad post Imran Khan ‘Azadi March’.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Did Rajasthan CM Gehlot Give This Statement About Lord... A video is being widely shared on social media, claiming that Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot has ‘insulted’ Lord Ram. In the viral clip, Ashok Gehlot can be heard saying that ‘Ra’ in Ram means Lord Ram and ‘M’ means Mohammed.The video is shared on Facebook with a Hindi caption: “राम में जो रा है उसका मतलब राम है और राम में जो म है उसका मतलब मोहम्मद है :- अशोक गहलोत मुख्य मंत्री राजस्थान कब तक यह लोग भगवान राम का इस तरह से अपमान करेंगे?” (English translation: RA in Ram means Ram and M in Ram means Mohammad: Ashok Gehlot, Chief Minister of Rajasthan. How long will these people insult Lord Ram like this?)Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKWhen NewsMobile fact-checked the above claim, it was found to be MISLEADING.Using the InVid Tool, we extracted keyframes from the viral video and performed a Reverse Image Search with relevant keywords. This search directed us to a news report published by Bhaskar on May 28, 2022. According to the report, Chief Minister Gehlot participated in a programme organised at Dariyav Dham Ren, head bench of the Ramsnehi sect in Nagaur, Rajasthan. Gehlot said: “Dariyav ji Maharaj had mentioned that the Ra in Ram means Ram and the M in Ram means Mohammed. The symbol of such Hindu-Muslim unity was Dariyav ji Maharaj.”Searching further, we found the video of the event uploaded on the official YouTube account of Chief Minister Gehlot on May 28, 2022. In the 41:20-minute video, Gehlot reads with a paper in his hand: “Dariyav ji Maharaj had said that the word ‘RA’ in Ram means Ram and the ‘M’ means Mohammed. The symbol of such Hindu-Muslim unity was Dariyav ji Maharaj.”Thus, it is evident from the above information that Chief Minister Gehlot was speaking while quoting Dariyav ji Maharaj. Hence, the viral post is misleading.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 979l9Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos n our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: This Video Doesn’t Show Delhi IAS Officer’s Reaction After... A video of a lady complaining is being shared on social media with a claim that she is the Delhi IAS officer, who walked her dog at Delhi stadium. The post claims that this was her reaction after finding out that she has been transferred to Arunachal Pradesh, while her husband has been transferred to Ladakh.The Facebook post reads: “सड़ जी की चहेती, कुत्ते वाली IAS मैडम ट्रांसफर आर्डर मिलने के बाद….खिलाड़ियों को स्टेडियम खाली करा कुत्ता घुमाने वक्त शर्म नहीं आई थी इन पढ़े लिखे जाहिलो को…?”Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the post, and found it to be false.While analysing the video carefully, we noticed the text ‘Native Media PK beside the Twitter logo at the bottom right corner. We scanned through their Twitter page and found the original video which was posted on May 24, 2022.The Urdu caption can be translated into English as: “1/2 #PakistanNeedsStabilityToday the team #NativeMedia asked people for their opinion on how they view the kind of #Sexist remarks that @ImranKhanPTI passed in the Multan meeting. The majority opinion will be uploaded tonight. Here is a sample of #InternalizedMisogyny. Full video link: https://youtu.be/9_W_XRnef4I”The 4:31-minute video was also published on their YouTube channel. In the video, she is saying that she supports Imran Khan. The viral clip has been taken 1 min 48 sec of the video, where she was talking about a police raid on the house of the daughter-in-law of Pakistani poet Allama Muhammad Iqbal, former justice Nasira Iqbal.Hence, from the above fact-check it is clear that the video of a lady from Pakistan is being shared with false claims.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: 2016 JPSC PT Result News Clip Falsely Circulated As... The Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) declared result of the Combined Civil Services (Mains) 2021, recently. Soon after, a picture of a news article started making the rounds on social media.The headline of the report read that a general (category) candidate with a score of 210 passed, while an OBC (category) candidate with a 259 score failed the examination.Here’s the link to the above post.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the post, and found it to be old.While looking for similar posts, we found that a Facebook user shared the same picture in March 2020.Moreover, the sub-heads of the report mentioned the ‘6th JPSC PT‘ result. The exam for the same took place in 2016 and the first set of results was declared in 2017.We then ran a keyword search and found a report by Dainik Bhaskar five years ago (2017), mentioning that after the results were declared, candidates protested outside the JPSC office against the passing of general category students in PT, who scored lesser marks than the reserved category students.As per the report, the students said that the general category students, who scored 210 marks, were passed in PT, while those who got 259 marks from the reserved category failed.We also found a report by Live Hindustan, dated June 7, 2021, mentioning that the recruitment process for the 6th JPSC PT, which started in October 2016, got completed in April 2020, due to an issue with the result.On searching further, we also found reports dated February 2022, stating that ‘The Jharkhand High Court has scrapped the final result of the Sixth Combined Civil Services examination, conducted by Jharkhand Public Services Commission (JPSC) in 2016, rendering the appointment of all 326 successful candidates null and void’. The reports can be seen here and here.Hence, it is clear now that the viral article clipping is old and not related to the 2021 results, which were announced recently.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Video of Police Using Batons Against SP Workers Falsely... A commission was appointed by a court in Varanasi to conduct a survey of the Kashi Vishwanath temple-Gyanvapi Mosque complex in Uttar Pradesh. The survey started on April 26, 2022. Before the survey began, many people offered namaz at the Gyanvapi mosque, and when the survey team entered the complex, around 50 people started protesting. In response, Hindu groups mobilised and chanted religious slogans, raising tensions in the area. Police finally removed the protesters.In the above context, many social media users are sharing a video of police using batons against some people. The video is shared with a caption hinting that it shows police beating those protesting against the Gyanvyapi mosque survey.The caption associated with the video reads: “बोल रहे थे ज्ञानवापी में सर्वे नहीं होने देंगे फिर क्या था उ.प्र. पुलिस सुजाने मे इतना टाइम नहीं लगाती है.” (English translation: They were saying that surveys will not be allowed in Gyanvapi,, but UP police don’t take that much time — to take action.)The link to the post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile did the fact-check, and found the claim to be misleading.On doing a Google Reverse Image Search with one of the keyframes of the viral video, we found a similar image was shared by Navbharat Times on July 5, 2021. The report associated with the video said that police lathi-charged Samajwadi Party workers. The workers were protesting against the favours the administration had allegedly extended to the ruling party candidates during the Zila Panchayat elections in UP.We also found that the same video was uploaded by the official Twitter handle of the Samajwadi Party on July 3, 2021, with a caption: “प्रयागराज में मुख्यमंत्री के आदेश पर सपा कार्यकर्ताओं पर पुलिस का बर्बर लाठीचार्ज घोर निंदनीय! सत्ता के दमन से मिली जीत का खोखला जश्न ज्यादा दिन तक न चल पाएगा। प्रदेश का युवा, किसान, महिलाएं, बेटियां 2022 में सपा सरकार बनायेंगे।” (English translation: The barbaric lathi charge of police on SP workers on the orders of UP chief minister in Prayagraj is highly condemnable! The hollow celebration of victory achieved by suppression of power will not last long. The youth, farmers, women, and daughters of the state will form the SP government in 2022.)Hence, it can be concluded that the video is quite old and is widely being shared with misleading claims.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: 2019 Picture Of Major Vibhuti Shankar’s Funeral Resurfaces As... A picture has surfaced on the internet with a claim that the picture is of the funeral of Major Vibhuti Shankar who was martyred (today).The caption in Hindi read: “8 महीने पहले हुई थी शादी 😢मां बाप के एकलौता पुत्र थे मेजर विभूति शंकर जी 😭😭और आज इनकी पत्नी विधवा हो गई ।”(English Translation: “Got married 8 months ago. Major Vibhuti Shankar was the only son of his parents and today his wife became a widow.”)The above post can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above post and found it to be misleading.On putting the picture through Google Reverse Image Search, we found several reports from 2019 where the same image was featured. According to reports, the picture is from the funeral of Major Vibhuti Shankar who was martyred on February 18, 2019, during an operation in Jammu and Kashmir’s Pulwama in which five terrorists were killed and 200 kg of explosives were recovered.It is to be noted that in May 2021, Major Vibhuti Shankar’s wife Nitika Kaul was commissioned into the Indian Army.Meanwhile, on November 22, 2021, Major Vibhuti Shankar Dhoundiyal was honoured with Shaurya Chakra and his wife Lieutenant Nitika Kaul and mother Saroj Dhoundiyal receive his award.#WATCH | Delhi: Major Vibhuti Shankar Dhoundiyal’s wife Lieutenant Nitika Kaul and mother Saroj Dhoundiyal receive his Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous) for an operation in Jammu and Kashmir in which five terrorists were killed and 200 kg explosives were recovered. pic.twitter.com/0TmNwgBQ3b — ANI (@ANI) November 22, 2021Hence, in conclusion, we can say that the picture in question is old and has resurfaced with a misleading claim.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: Did Pfizer CEO Say ‘By 2023, He Want To... A video of Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla, speaking at the World Economic Forum, is being circulated on social media platforms. It claims that while speaking, he said that by 2023, he wish to reduce the world population by 50%.The video is being shred with the caption: “2023 तक हम विश्व में लोगों की संख्या को 50% कम कर पाएंगे! यह हमारा एक अहम गोल या मकसद था!’* *वर्ल्ड इकोनॉमिक फोरम (WEF) के मंच से साफ-साफ!* *सवाल है कैसे करेंगे ? क्यों करेंगे ?**सवालात पूछने बजाए सामने बैठे लोग तालियाँ बजा रहे!!”(English translation: By 2023, we will be able to reduce the number of people in the world by 50%! This was an important goal of ours! From the forum of the World Economic Forum (WEF)! The question is how will you do it? Why would you? Instead of asking questions, people sitting in front are clapping.)In the video, Bourla can be heard saying: “I think that is really fulfilling of a dream that we had together with our leadership team when we started in ’19. The first week we met in January of ’19 in California to set up the goals for the next five years and one of them was by 2023, we will reduce the number of people in the world by 50 per cent. I think today, this dream is becoming a reality.”The above video can be seen here.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the post and found the video to be altered.We ran a keyword search but did not find any credible media report corroborating the viral claim. Had Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla actually said it, it would have made headlines.We then scanned through the YouTube channel of the World Economic Forum for the original video, and found that the video of the conversation between Klaus Schwab, WEF Founder and Chairman and Albert Bourla, which was uploaded on May 25, 2022.We listened to the video carefully and found that the viral clip was taken from 2:34 min into the video and was edited to create a false narrative.In the original video, he says: “I think that is really fulfilling of a dream that we had together with our leadership team when we started in ’19. The first week we met, in January of ’19 in California, and set up the goals for the next five years. And one of them was by 2023 we will reduce the number of people in the world that cannot afford our medicines by 50%. I think today this dream is becoming reality.”The line ‘that cannot afford our medicines‘ was removed from the original video to make it seem like he is talking about reducing the world population.Hence, from the above fact check, it is clear that the viral video is edited and is being shared with a false claim.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news

content: Fact Check: No, This Is Not The Illustration of India’s First... A picture of an underwater rail-cum-road network has surfaced on the Internet with a claim that it is India’s first underwater road-and-rail line, which is being built in Assam under the Brahmaputra river.The caption in Hindi reads: “इसे कहते हैं नया भारत…..भारत की पहली पानी के नीचे सड़क व रेलवे लाइन, यह असम में ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी के नीचे बनी लगभग 14 किलोमीटर लंबी सुरंग है। – जय हो” (English translation: This is called New India… India’s first underwater road and railway line. It is approximately 14-km long tunnel built under the Brahmaputra river in Assam. – Jai Ho)The post can be seen here.At the time of filing this report, the above post had been shared over 9,000 times.FACT CHECKNewsMobile fact-checked the above post, and found it to be misleading.By putting the picture through Google Lens, we found that several news articles have also featured the same image.The reports suggested that the illustration in question is of the Fehmarn Belt Fixed Link project, which connects Germany and Denmark with an underwater rail-and-road link.The caption of the picture read: “When completed, the underwater auto and rail tunnel will connect Germany and Denmark. (Image: Femern A/S)”However, on digging further, we also found reports suggesting that India’s Railway Ministry and Road Transport Ministry along with the Border Road Organisation (BRO) are planning to construct the country’s first underwater road-cum-rail tunnels across the Brahmaputra river to connect Assam and Arunachal Pradesh with an estimated cost of ₹7,000 crores.But, the Indian government is yet to release any illustrations or pictures of the project.In conclusion, the illustration in question is not of India’s first underwater rail-road project.If you want to fact-check any story, WhatsApp it now on +91 11 7127 9799Your nameYour emailSubjectYour message (optional)ΔClick here for Latest News updates and viral videos on our AI-powered smart news
