content: Fact Check: Bogus Defence Ministry letter about Agnipath Scheme goes viral with false claims Amid the widespread protest against the Centre's Agnipath Scheme for short-term recruitment in the armed forces, a letter purportedly from the Ministry of Defence is making the rounds on social media. Per the letter, personnel under Other Ranks (ORs) attested after January 1, 2019, and “not promoted to a substantive rank of Naik or equivalent” on July 1 “are to be kept under the Agnipath Scheme.”advertisementOne such post can be seen below.AFWA also received multiple requests to fact-check this letter on our WhatsApp tipline number. In our investigation, we found that the letter in circulation is fake. The Ministry of Defence has not released any such letter regarding the Agnipath Scheme.AFWA probeThe letter in question was signed by MK Ramanna, Additional Secretary to GoI. However, we couldn’t find any officer by that name in the rank of Additional Secretary on the Ministry of Defence website. The officer's telephone number in the letter also doesn’t exist.Moreover, had the ministry released such a letter, it would have definitely made the news. But we couldn’t find any report that said any such thing.AFWA then reached out to Army spokesperson Sudhir Chamoli, who confirmed that the letter was fake. The fact-check wing of the Press Information Bureau also tweeted saying the Ministry of Defence did not release any such letter regarding the Agnipath Scheme.Claim: ORs attested after 1 Jan 2019 & those not promoted to a substantive rank of Naik or equivalent on 1 July 2022 are to be kept under #AgnipathScheme #PIBFactCheckThis letter is #Fake@DefenceMinIndia has not issued this letter pic.twitter.com/79SEUU1hHv — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) June 20, 2022Agnipath is a new scheme by the government of India for the recruitment of youths (between the ages of seventeen-and-a-half and 23) into the armed forces for a period of four years. Those selected under this scheme would form a distinct rank that would be different from any other existing ranks.It is thus clear that the letter in circulation is bogus and not released by the Ministry of Defence.(With inputs from Yash Mittal)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Woman in this photo is Kerala student leader, not Rana Ayyub An image is being virally shared on social media with the claim that it shows journalist Rana Ayyub being picked up by the police during a protest. It showed a sloganeering lady being forcibly taken away by police personnel in what seemed to be a road picketing."Jinnah was always right ..what a brave girl ..salute to her courage Rana Ayyub may ALLAH be with her," the viral image was captioned by multiple users.advertisementThe post was shared by many, including verified Twitter handles.Jinnah was always right ..what a brave girl ..salute to her courage @RanaAyyub may ALLAH be with her pic.twitter.com/qD1eNv34iE — Shaan Shahid (@mshaanshahid) June 14, 2022Similar claims have been archived here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. The lady in the image is not Rana Ayyub, but student activist Aysha Renna. The photo was taken in Kerala's Malappuram earlier in June.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the photo took us to the Facebook page 'Fraternity Movement Kerala'. The Fraternity Movement is the student's wing of the political outfit Welfare Party of India.The page had several Malayalam news reports that had used the now viral photo. They had collected several news reports of a police crackdown on a protest arranged by their members in Malappuram district on June 12. As per these reports, it showed national secretary Aysha Renna being manhandled by the Kerala Police.As per these reports, the Fraternity organised the protest to condemn the UP police action against their leader, Afreen Fatima. Activist Afreen Fatima's house in Prayagraj was razed to the ground by the UP government. This came after Afreen's father, Javed Mohammad, was named by the UP police among the conspirators of the June 10 violence that saw stone pelting and the torching of vehicles.On Aysha's Facebook handle, a poster of the 'National Highway Blockade' in Malappuram on June 12 was retrieved.We found several television reports that confirmed that the woman in the video is Aysha Renna and not Rana Ayyub.After confirming the protestor's identity, we checked to see if the police had arrested Rana Ayyub for any public protest. However, there has been no recent information on the same.This helped us to conclude that it is the photo of a student protest from Kerala that is being shared as that of police action against journalist Rana Ayyub.
label: rumor

content: Fact check video: How a 2020 letter from Amit Shah has become a template for fraud claims A letter from Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s office to Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami about Nupur Sharma’s security detail has gone viral on social media.India Today's Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the letter to be fake. Similar fake letters in Amit Shah’s name, using the same template, have gone viral in the past.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old RRB-NTPC protest video used to assert RJD's role behind anti-Agnipath violence Several states like Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar have witnessed violent protests against the recent introduction of the 'Agnipath' scheme. Agitations turned violent and resulted in damage to public property worth hundreds of crores in Bihar.The main opposition party of Bihar, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) has also supported the ongoing protest. Meanwhile, a video has gone viral on social media questioning RJD's role in prompting the youth to riot.advertisementIn the viral video, a man is heard introducing himself as a follower of Lalu Prasad Yadav-- the RJD patron, while talking to the press. He goes on to voice the concerns of the students but loses words and disappears when asked about the cause of the protest.While sharing the video, Twitter users have posted captions that blame the party, whose leader is convicted of 'fodder scams', for orchestrating the ongoing protests.Archived versions of the similar claims can be seen here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found these posts to be misleading as the video is not related to the ongoing protest. The video is from January when Bihar witnessed protests over the two-stage RRB-NTPC exams.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the screenshots from the viral clip led us to the same video posted by a Twitter user on January 31, 2022.In that video, the logo of 'Principle of News' was visible. We ran some keywords and found the YouTube channel 'Principle of News' that covers the developments in Bihar.We found the original video uploaded on January 28, 2022, from which the viral clip was snipped out. The caption of the video clearly states this protest on the RRB-NTPC row.What was the protest about?This is not the first time that Bihar has seen students' protests going violent and leading to arson of public properties this year. In January, angry students set trains on fire after the Railways decided to hold the Railway Recruitment Board's Non-Technical Popular Categories (RRB-NTPC) exams 2021 in two stages. The agitators claimed the second stage for final selection was tantamount to "cheating" those who appeared and cleared the first stage of the RRB-NTPC for computer-based test (CBT) which was released on January 15.Meanwhile, the Agnipath scheme was introduced by the government on June 14, 2022. Since then, the RJD has urged the central government several times to recall this scheme.Therefore, it is safe to conclude that the viral video is not related to the ongoing protests. The footage from several months before is now shared with misleading claims.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Russia’s lost ships in the war against Ukraine but this US vessel is not one of them A video has gone viral on social media that allegedly shows a missile strike on a Russian ship while at the sea. The video did not, however, mention where the ship was attacked or who attacked it.A video that allegedly shows a missile strike on a Russian ship at sea has gone viral on social media. India Today's Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the video to be old.This video shows a sinking exercise performed on a decommissioned US ship during the 2016 Rim of the Pacific drill.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Are senior citizen concessions back in Indian Railways? Viral post is a hoax Will the Indian Railways resume the concessions for senior citizens from July? A viral message on social media claims that from July 1, the Indian Railways will resume discounting tickets for senior citizens. Per the post the concessions will be 40 per cent for males above the age of 60 and 50 per cent for females above the age of 58.advertisementThis post and similar ones have been shared by many on Facebook.AFWA found that the viral claim is a hoax. No such decision has been announced by the Indian Railways or the Ministry of Railways.The viral posts have been archived here and here.Ministry of Railways says noIndia Today went straight to the horse’s mouth and contacted Rajeev Jain, ADG Public Relations, Ministry of Railways. Jain categorically denied this viral post, calling it “fake news”. He said, “No such decision has been taken, there will be no change in concessions from July 1. Only the existing concessions will continue.”On May 19, this year while speaking to reporters at IIT Madras, Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the concession for senior citizens could not be resumed because the Railways was already operating at a subsidised rate.“For every Rs. 100 spent towards operational expenses, the Railways collects only Rs. 45 from a passenger. We have to contribute to keeping the railways a sustainable mode of transport,” the minister emphasised.Who started this rumour?A Facebook page named "Rail Mail" claimed in a post that the Indian Railways was set to resume concession for the elderly starting July 1. However, the Facebook page later retracted its claim and apologised for its error.On June 11, a Twitter user raised a query about the concession for the elderly, to which the official Twitter account of Railway Seva replied, "Presently concessions are being given to 4 categories of Divyangjan, and 11 categories of Patients and Students," reinstating that the claim about the resumption of concessions for elderly was false.What are the present concessions in place?Indian Railways concessions used to range from 25 per cent to 100 per cent in 53 categories. The details of these concessions can be seen here.But in view of the pandemic and Covid-19 protocols, with effect from March 20, 2020, the Railways indefinitely discontinued concessions with exception to only four categories of Divyangjan, 11 categories of patients, and students. In March this year, the Railway Minister said in the Lok Sabha that the ministry had no plans to restore the concessions for senior citizens.advertisementEven the Press Information Bureau fact-checked this claim and tweeted that posts like these had no factual basis.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: A tale of three letters - How a 2020 letter from Amit Shah has become a template for fraud claims Immediately following her controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad, Nupur Sharma reportedly received numerous threats online. The former Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson’s comments have been the subject of international and national outrage.Amid violent protests against her, several FIRs, and reported death threats, a photo of a letter has been making the rounds that supposedly shows the government providing her family with high-level security.advertisementThe purported letter from Home Minister Amit Shah asks Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami to provide Z security to Sharma’s family home in Dehradun. The letter also praises Sharma for promoting the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ideology and working towards the ultimate goal of a “Hindu Rashtra”.One such post can be seen below.AFWA found that the letter in circulation is bogus. The Home Ministry has not asked the Uttarakhand CM to provide Z security to Nupur Sharma.Same letter, new hoaxWe couldn’t find any media report about Shah writing a letter to Dhami regarding Sharma’s security. If the Home Minister had written such a letter, it would have made the news.On June 14, the Press Information Bureau tweeted that Shah sent no such letter to Dhami.A letter is doing rounds on social media claiming to be written by Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, to CM of Uttarakhand, Pushkar Singh Dhami.#PIBFactCheckThis letter is FAKENo such letter has been issued by @HMOIndiaDo not share the letter pic.twitter.com/uHM5KGhu3j — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) June 14, 2022This isn’t the first time fake letters in the name of Shah have gone viral. We compared the now-viral letter to another phoney letter that went viral in 2021, supposedly sent by Shah to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.Both letters had the same serial number, “28647021”. But there were other glaring similarities as well. Similar shadows in the centre, a dent at the bottom of the letter, and identical folds and creases in two different parts of the letters were visible.Despite these blatant similarities, however, we also noticed some inconsistencies. The placement of Shah’s signature is different in both letters. So, we used error level analysis (ELA), a forensic method that can highlight digitally-modified portions of an image.We uploaded both letters to FotoForensics. The website highlighted in white the parts of both letters — 2021 and 2022 — which were edited. The body text of the letters was highlighted as edited, as were the sign-offs. The ELA, however, revealed that the signature of the Home Minister, the national emblem or the details in the header and footer were not digitally altered.This is the 2021 letter.This is the 2022 letter.Tracing the original letterThe ELA analysis revealed that in both letters, the same parts were unaltered. Plus, both letters shared similar physical attributes. Thus, we deduced that there was likely an original letter that was edited to create the fraudulent ones.Advanced searches led us to the letter. A September 2020 report in “TrueScoop” carried a letter from Amit Shah’s office that had multiple visual elements similar to the bogus letters.This letter was a response from Shah’s office to Maharashtra BJP MLA Nitesh Narayan Rane who had written to the MHA requesting security for Disha Salian’s partner Rohan Rai. Salian, who was found dead in June 2020, was the former manager of Sushant Singh Rajput. When India Today reached out to Rane, the MLA confirmed that the 2020 letter was real and was sent to him by Shah’s office in 2020.The serial number in Rane’s letter was 1864702. The serial numbers in the 2021 and 2022 letters were 28647021. It is clear that in both subsequent letters, the serial numbers were slightly tweaked.advertisementIt is noteworthy that in 2021, MHA officials confirmed to India Today that no letter bearing the serial number “28647021” had been issued by them.Thus, we concluded that the 2022 letter where Shah asked Dhami to provide Z security to Sharma is bogus. The original letter that was digitally altered was issued by Shah’s office to Maharashtra MLA Nitesh Rane in 2020.(With inputs from Pathikrit Sanyal)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: This video of cop thrashing elderly man is NOT from anti-Nupur Sharma protests, it’s from 2020 In the backdrop of ongoing protests surrounding Nupur Sharma's controversial remarks on Prophet Muhammad and police action by the Uttar Pradesh government against the protesters, a video of a man being thrashed by police has gone viral with the claim that “Hindutva radicalised cops” brutally assaulted an elderly Muslim man.Many on Twitter shared the video where a masked policeman could be seen chasing and thrashing a bearded man with a baton. As the video continued, more officers could also be seen beating up others. The video was shared with hashtags like #AfreenFatima, #MuslimsUnderAttackinIndia, and #MuslimLivesMatter.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room found that the viral video is two years old and not related to the recent Nupur Sharma controversy. It shows cops punishing people for not following lockdown protocols in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh.The viral posts are archived here and here.AFWA ProbeA reverse image search on Yandex led us to the same video being shared as early as 2020. Several YouTube channels uploaded a longer version of the viral video in April 2020, mentioning it was from Bareilly.Subsequent searches narrowed down to the aforementioned date and location led us to a News Nation video report. Titled, “Uttar Pradesh: Police Attacked By A Group In Bareilly While Enforcing Lockdown,” the report was from April 7, 2020.Per the report, during the Covid-19 lockdown in April 2020, people from the Izatnagar locality in Bareilly attacked a patrolling police party and violated lockdown protocols. Later, a larger group of policemen raided the area and lathi-charged people violating lockdown norms.This incident was reported by several mainstream media outlets in 2020 which can be seen here, here, and here.Recently, following Nupur Sharma’s controversial remarks, nationwide protests took place and some of these protests turned violent. However, the viral video is not related to the ongoing row. It’s a two-year-old video from Bareilly.(With input from Sanjana Saxena)
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Is this Nupur Sharma’s response to international backlash? Nope, this video is from 2019 The Nupur Sharma row continues to unfold. From death threats to several FIRs to public interest litigation in the Supreme Court, Sharma’s controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad have caused a storm.Amid all this, a video has gone viral with the claim that, despite all the drama, the now-suspended Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson appears fairly nonchalant — defiant even — in the face of all the opposition. The video shows Sharma and a group of people shouting, “How’s the Josh?” followed by, “High, sir!” They also chant, “Jai Hind!” a couple of times.advertisementThose sharing the video wrote captions like, “This is what you call, rub salt into wounds. We are proud of the lioness, Nupur Sharma,” and, “Queen After Offending 1 Billion.”The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was false. The video is from 2019 and has no connection with the ongoing row.AFWA ProbeWhile investigating the claim, we first reverse-searched frames from the video and found the original video on Sharma’s verified Twitter account. She shared it on January 26, 2019.The caption of the video read: “Celebrating Republic Day and URI - The Surgical Strike with old college friends!” Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Bollywood actor Vicky Kaushal were also tagged in the tweet.The film “Uri: The Surgical Strike” directed by Aditya Dhar, was released in January 2019. Aside from Kaushal, the film's star cast included Paresh Rawal, Mohit Raina, and Yami Gautam. The plot revolves around the death of 19 soldiers during a terrorist attack at the army headquarters in Uri, Jammu and Kashmir, and the Indian Army’s subsequent retaliation.Hence, we concluded that this video has no connection with the ongoing Nupur Sharma row following her comments on the Prophet Muhammad. The video is from January 26, 2019.(With inputs from Yash Mittal)
label: truth

content: Fact Check Video: Khargone Ram Navami violence clip shared as from anti-Nupur Sharma protest Following countrywide (sometimes violent) protests against controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad, social media has been abuzz with videos and photos supposedly capturing said violence. Different people have accused Hindus, Muslims, and even the police of instigating violence.Among such media is the footage of a group, some donning saffron, pelting stones from the roof of a house.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. The video was not shot during the protests over the comments made by now-suspended BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma. It showed the clashes that broke out in Madhya Pradesh's Khargone in April 2022 during Ram Navami celebrations.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Russia’s lost ships in the war against Ukraine but this decommissioned US vessel is not one of them The Russian navy has reportedly taken several high-profile losses while battling Ukraine since February 2022. Putin's naval forces have so far lost at least several “Raptor” patrol boats, a landing ship, a landing craft, and most notably the Moskva, the flagship of its Black Sea Fleet.As the invasion wages on, a video has gone viral on social media that allegedly shows a missile strike on a Russian ship while at the sea. The video did not, however, mention where the ship was attacked or who attacked it.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was false. This video shows a sinking exercise performed on a decommissioned US ship during the 2016 Rim of the Pacific drill.AFWA ProbeReverse-searching the video’s keyframes on Yandex revealed plenty of results. The top result was an article in popularmechanics.com that featured the same video. The headline for the July 2016 story said, “Watch the Navy Send a Retired Frigate Out With a Bang.” The article said the video showed the US Navy along with its allies sinking an old frigate as part of a drill in the Pacific Ocean.While the article confirmed that the video was not recent, we checked for more credible sources to confirm the origin of the video.On the verified YouTube channel called 'AiirSource Military', we found a longer version of the viral video.The video was titled, “Sinking A Navy Frigate With Missiles And Torpedoes SINKEX Sinking Exercise,” and it was uploaded to the channel on July 17, 2016. The description of the video reads, "Aerial video of the sinking exercise (SINKEX) of the decommissioned USS Thach (FFG 43) during Rim of the Pacific 2016. The decommissioned ship is fired at with missiles and torpedoes until they sink."Following this, we ran a keyword search for the Rim of the Pacific or RIMPAC 2016, the world's largest international maritime warfare exercise. According to the Daily Mail, decommissioned ships are stripped of their weapons and used for target practice by the forces of the US, Canada, Australia, and South Korea during the biennial event. The report, which had images of the frigate being taken out in plenty, stated the naval and air units of the United Forces took 12 hours to sink the 2013-retired USS Thach near the Hawaiian Islands.According to news.usni.org, on July 14, 2016, the old frigate fell prey to the missiles and torpedoes of the four allies. CNN's video story on the same that used similar footage can be seen here.Thus, it became clear that the claim that the video showed an attack on a Russian ship was baseless. It showed the sinking of an old US frigate as part of the RIMPAC drills in 2016.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check Video: Old video of UP police from Etawah goes viral linking it to Kanpur violence This special report takes viewers onto the sets of the upcoming Tamil movie 'Parashakti', starring Shiva Karthikeyan, Ravi, and Sri Leela. The report notes that 'this movie is expected to touch the part because that anti-Hindi agitation paved the way for the Dravidian government'. Viewers get a glimpse of nostalgic elements from the period, including Goli Soda bottles, pull rickshaws, a vintage Chevrolet, and recreations of old railway and radio stations, all contributing to the historical setting of the film which is expected to release on Pongal 2026.

content: Fact Check: This video is from Khargone Ram Navami violence, NOT ongoing protests against Nupur Sharma Following countrywide (sometimes violent) protests against controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad, social media has been abuzz with videos and photos supposedly capturing said violence. Different people have accused Hindus, Muslims, and even the police of instigating violence.Among such media is the footage of a group, some donning saffron, pelting stones from the roof of a house. "People of Godsewadi rotten society are clearly visible pelting stones from the top of the roof at a peaceful protest. These are the people who start the real stone-pelting, and if Muslims defend themselves, the media and intelligentsia start talking of violence," a tweet that shared the video read.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. The video was not shot during the protests over the comments made by now-suspended BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma. It showed the clashes that broke out in Madhya Pradesh's Khargone in April 2022 during Ram Navami celebrations.AFWA ProbeWhile the post didn't mention where the video was from, a stamp at the bottom that read, “OPPO Reno6 5G 2022.04.10 18:13.” This is a standard feature in Oppo smartphones that can be optionally activated.If needed, the Oppo logo can be watermarked to media alongside the date and time of the shot, the phone’s model, or both. Thus, we could surmise that this video was possibly from the evening of April 10, 2022 — long before Sharma even made the offending comments.Reverse-searching keyframes of the video led us to a tweet from April 14. User Samiullah Khan claimed the video was from Madhya Pradesh's Khargone, and that it showed “Hindutva Extremists” pelting stones at Muslims in the Taudi Mohalla near Mata Chowk. This further confirmed that the video was old and unrelated to the ongoing protests.What happened in Khargone?Per reports, 175 people were arrested and 64 FIRs were filed after violence broke out in Khargone, Madhya Pradesh during Ram Navami celebrations on April 10 — the date in the video's watermark. The curfew imposed in the area was only lifted in May, almost 24 days after the violence.Nasir Ahmed Khan, a resident of the locality reportedly told Newschecker that his house came under attack from those seen in the video. An FIR was filed against eight people.India Today got in touch with a local, who under the condition of anonymity confirmed that the video was shot in the Taudi Mohalla neighbourhood of Mata Chowki in MP during the April unrest.advertisement''The group pelted stones from the roof. A police complaint was filed naming around 32 people and 8 were arrested. However, no such incident of violence has taken place in the area recently," he said.He shared recent photographs of the building from which the group is seen pelting stones in the video.With his help, we were also able to geolocate the house in question.Hence, we concluded that the viral video did not show violence during protests over Nupur Sharma's remarks. It’s from MP’s Khargone, where communal violence broke out earlier this year during Ram Navami.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in New Delhi)
label: truth

content: Fact Check Video: Lahore protestors burned the Tricolour over prophet row, not Indians The row over remarks against the Prophet Nabi by BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma refuses to die down even after days. Despite diplomatic pressure from several Muslim nations, protests have erupted in several states, resulting in police action.Among the videos and photos that are shared on social media of the protests, there is an image of a group burning an upturned Indian Tricolour.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. The photo was taken from Pakistan's Lahore on June 9 during a protest by religious groups over Sharma's remarks.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: This Kolkata cop was NOT killed by people protesting against Nupur Sharma Protests took place across several Indian cities on June 10 over Nupur Sharma’s controversial remarks on Prophet Muhammad. Police resorted to lathi-charge and used teargas to quell protests that turned violent.A shocking video supposedly from protests in Kolkata has gone viral with disturbing claims. The video showed a seemingly dead police officer drenched in blood, lying on a road with a rifle beside him. The video can be seen here. Warning: this video contains graphic footage and may be upsetting to some people.advertisementAn angry crowd was seen surrounding the body. While most voices were unintelligible because of the cacophony, people appeared to shout angrily at another policeman there. Those sharing the video claimed that a mob of protestors killed the policeman and threatened the other cop present at the scene.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the claim along with the video is misleading. While the video is from June 10, the officer seen in it shot himself dead after firing at multiple persons at Kolkata’s Park Circus.AFWA ProbeA Google search revealed photos and videos from the same incident carried in multiple media reports from June 10.Per the reports, at around 2.30 pm on June 10, Choudup Lepcha, a constable with the fifth battalion of the Kolkata Armed Police, fired about 10-15 rounds at the public. The incident took place at Lower Range Road, near the Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Park Circus, Kolkata, where the constable was posted.A woman on a bike taxi was killed in the onslaught. Two others were injured. Subsequently, the policeman died by suicide after shooting himself. We did not find any report that claims the constable was shot by anyone in the public.Vineet Kumar Goyal, the commissioner of Kolkata Police, told reporters that Lepcha was recruited in 2021 on compassionate grounds since his father died in service in 2017. He was on a ten-day leave and joined back only on June 9. The commissioner also said that the police were investigating why the constable opened fire and then shot himself.An India Today video report about the incident can be seen below:It is hence clear that the police officer seen in the video was not killed by protestors but died by suicide — he shot himself after opening fire at people. While we were unable to ascertain if the other policeman was being threatened by the crowd, it is likely that the people were only expressing their anger about the incident.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Did cops blame BJP for Kanpur violence? Old video viral with false claims Kanpur has recently witnessed mob violence followed by police lathi-charge over BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma’s controversial remarks on Prophet Muhammad.A total of 24 people were held and 800 were booked initially by the Uttar Pradesh police related to the incident.Now a video of a police officer talking over the phone has gone viral with the claim that Uttar Pradesh police are blaming the BJP for the recent violence in Kanpur. The police officer can be heard talking to someone saying, “BJP leaders along with the MLA have come with bombs”.advertisementMultiple Facebook users have posted this video alongside a caption in Hindi that translates to, “In Kanpur, the police themselves are saying that a BJP MLA has brought a bomb. He is telling this to one of his senior officers. But still, no one has been arrested, only innocent Muslims are being arrested.”India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) has found that this video is not related to the recent violence in Kanpur. In July 2021, during Uttar Pradesh's Block Pramukh elections, the SP (City) of Etawah district was allegedly slapped. The officer was caught on camera talking over the phone and saying he has been slapped.The viral posts are saved here and here.AFWA probeWith the help of a reverse image search, we found a Hindi news report published by NDTV India on July 10, 2021, along with a screenshot from the viral video.Per this report, a video of the Etawah City SP had gone viral during the UP panchayat elections, where he was heard complaining to his senior over the phone that BJP leaders had slapped him and they had gathered with bombs.Taking this as a clue, we ran keyword searches and found the longer version of the viral video on the YouTube channel, Mojo Story.This video was uploaded on July 10, last year. The video description reads, “During the counting of Uttar Pradesh's Block Pramukh elections, SP City of Etawah district was allegedly slapped. The SP City was caught on camera talking on a phone call and saying he has been slapped and the mob came with stones and bombs. He reportedly said that BJP MLA and District President were leading the mob.”The same video was also uploaded on another YouTube news channel and the incident was reported by mainstream news portals last year.Two BJP workers were arrested for allegedly slapping Prashant Kumar, the city SP of Etawah police, who is seen in the viral video talking on the phone.So it is clear that the viral video is not related to the recent Kanpur violence. It was shot during the Uttar Pradesh's Block Pramukh elections in Etawah in July 2021.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Two-year-old video of man threatening Muslims with guns goes viral amid Prophet row Amid the protests and controversies over the BJP's Nupur Sharma's remarks on Prophet Muhammad, a video has gone viral on social media where a man is seen threatening the Muslim community while firing a rifle.In the video (abusive language, viewers' discretion advised), a man in a red t-shirt is heard threatening to kill Muslims and abusing the Prophet. Later, he fires three rounds into the air. This clip was shared by many social media users with a caption that read, "Modi’s Hindus are now posting their promise to kill Muslims on social media with total impunity."advertisementCJ Werleman, correspondent of the Byline Times, shared this video quoting the same caption.Archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the posts to be misleading as the video is more than 2-years-old and is unrelated to the ongoing row. The man was arrested after the video went viral.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the screenshots from the viral clip led us to some older tweets of the same video. Abdul Shaik, a Twitter user, had posted a screengrab of the same video on April 26, 2020.It was the screenshot of a Facebook post from March 1, 2020. We ran the keywords of the caption on Facebook and found the same video was shared by many users between March 2020 and April 2020.After going through the comment section of such a video, we came across a newspaper cutting posted by a user named Malik Ansari. It was reported that the man in question was arrested for spreading provocative and abusive speech on social media.Who is this man?Using advanced Google search, we found multiple news stories from March 2020 about the incident. Articles from ETV Bharat, News18, and Hindustan confirmed that Yogendra Singh Chauhan was arrested in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh on March 1, 2020, by the Thakurgunj police.According to these reports, police recovered two air pistols and two air guns from Chauhan. A mobile phone was also seized from him.Seeking more details on Chauhan, we reached out to Hari Shankar, the SHO of Thakurgunj Police Station. While talking to AFWA he said, "This video is more than two years old. He was granted bail four months after his arrest. Chauhan went back to his native village, Sitapur and has been living there since then."Therefore, it is safe to conclude that the video going viral on social media claiming to be recent was shot in 2020. Also, the man got arrested following this incident.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Is Qatar deporting Hindu migrant workers after Nupur Sharma's controversial remarks? This video is from March Beyond a well-publicised condemnation of remarks made by now-suspended BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma, have there been material consequences for Indians living in Qatar? One viral video seems to suggest so.The video shows a large group of men standing outside a building. The claim alongside suggests the peninsular Arab country is deporting Hindus back to India in the wake of Sharma's controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad.advertisementIn the video, a man said that around 7,000 men were boarding a bus to buy tickets. He referred to the place as "Redco International".AFWA found that this video was from March, well before this controversy came into existence, and was thus unrelated to it.AFWA ProbeWe searched for “Redco International” on YouTube. The same video was shared by the channel QN Qatar on March 29, confirming that it was unrelated to the recent row.In March, the channel also published other videos of men in front of the same area. In another video, several men argued about their pending salaries with another man. We also found a video from March 26 where a man spoke to others in front of a building with the board “Redco International”. The description of the video reads, “Redco international company Qatar salary breaking news.”We also found similar videos of protests against Redco International uploaded to Facebook in March.While we couldn’t find any credible reports on Indians, particularly Hindus, getting fired by any of the Muslim-majority countries in the wake of Nupur Sharma’s remarks, we could conclude that this video was not related to the ongoing row.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Did a Congress leader from Hyderabad marry his daughter? Old hoax resurfaces A shocking Facebook post about a supposed Congress Party member has been making the rounds. The text in the post claims Ayub Khan of Hyderabad married his daughter Tharnum Khan. It also contained the photo of a newspaper report whose headline said: “Muslim man married own daughter, impregnates her."AFWA investigated the post and found it to be misleading. While the newspaper clipping is about a 2017 incident in West Bengal's Jalpaiguri, the claim about Ayub Khan marrying his daughter is an old hoax.The origin of the hoaxadvertisementWe found that the claim Ayub Khan married his daughter has been on the internet for at least two years now. Independent fact-checkers in 2020 called out a social media influencer, Tharnum Khan, for circulating the hoax.On her Facebook account, she shared photos of herself in a bridal costume. The caption of the photos read, “Got Married with my Dad Ayub Khan. I’m nervous. I don’t have marriage experience.”In fact, she changed the caption of the photos several times, finally settling on “White Attire”. She had tagged Ayub Khan to the post. But his Facebook profile was later deleted.Scanning through her social media accounts, we also found several videos where she mentions her supposed relationships with public figures. In one such video she referred to herself as the wife of cricketer Virat Kohli.Who is Ayub Khan?According to media reports, Ayub Khan, also known as Ayub Pahelwan, is a wanted criminal and gangster from Hyderabad. Speaking to The Logical Indian in November 2020, Khan’s son said that his father had five sons and no daughters. This puts the claims about him marrying his daughter to rest.Is he a Congress leader?We found a video from 2018 where Khan announced contesting the 2019 Telangana Assembly Election from Bahadurpura on a Congress ticket.However, in August 2018, a local court in Hyderabad sentenced the gangster along with his wife to seven years in prison in a fake passport case. The Telangana High Court granted him an interim bail for 15 days in February this year.Also, per MyNeta, Shaik Mohd Kalemmuddin was the Congress candidate in Bahadurpura in 2019.The news reportThe newspaper report shared in the viral post was about a Muslim man called Afazuddin, who married his daughter. However, the news report was from 2017. The same report was published by the Times of India in November 2017.Thus, we conclude that Ayub Khan, an imprisoned gangster and a supposed member of the Congress party, did not marry his daughter.(With inputs from Yash Mittal)
label: rumor
