content: Fact Check: Heard of the jealous Qatari man who sealed his wife’s genitals with glue? It’s satire Qatar has been a trending issue on social media of late. While many Muslim-majority nations have taken a stand against controversial remarks made by now-suspended BJP national spokesperson Nupur Sharma, supporters of the ruling party have taken particular umbrage at Qatar.Amid thousands of tweets calling out the country’s supposed hypocrisy on “blasphemy” and calls to boycott Qatar Airways, one odd post stuck out. It was a screenshot of an alleged report about a Qatari man who purportedly sealed his wife’s genitals with glue to punish her.advertisementThe headline in the screenshot read: “Qatar: Jealous husband seals wife’s vagina with crazy glue.”Through this screenshot, people are taking a dig at Qatar and its residents. A Twitter user shared this photo with the caption, “Just halal things next door”.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that this story was from a satirical news website. It wasn’t a real news report.AFWA ProbeUpon close inspection of the screenshot, we noticed “worldnewsdailyreport.com” written at the bottom. Subsequently, we searched for the story on the website and found it.The report said a 33-year-old man confessed before a court that he glued his wife’s genitals shut alleging she had adulterous ideas because she liked a post of his 12-year-old cousin on Facebook and also uploaded a selfie. The judge sentenced the wife to 100 lashes and fined the man 40 riyals or USD 10.It is noteworthy that the website’s tagline reads, “Where facts don’t matter.”The website’s ‘About’ section claims that it is an “American Jewish Zionist newspaper based in Tel Aviv and dedicated on covering biblical archaeology news and other mysteries around the Globe,” adding its staff includes “retired Mossad agents and veterans of the Israeli Armed Forces.”The ‘About’ section on the site’s Facebook page , however, says in loud and clear terms that it’s an independent satirical media organisation. It also states, “All characters appearing in the articles in this website — even those based on real people — are entirely fictional and any resemblance between them and any person, living, dead or undead, is purely a miracle.”Incidentally, this screenshot had also gone viral in 2017. At the time, many mainstream news websites including India Today and Aaj Tak reported on this, mistaking the satirical report for real news. These reports were later retracted.To sum it up, an old screenshot of a satirical news article is now being circulated as a real news report amid anti-Qatar social media trends in India.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Viral 'Boycott Qatar 2022' banner at stadium has nothing to do with Nupur Sharma While several countries — particularly Muslim-majority nations — have condemned the remarks made by Nupur Sharma on the Prophet Muhammad, social media trends indicate that Qatar in particular has earned the wrath of Indians. Trends like “Qatar Exposed” and “Boycott Qatar Airways” dominated Twitter.With that in the background, one photo has been shared widely that deserves to be examined. The photo shows a “Boycott Qatar 2022” banner being raised at a stadium. People sharing the photo claimed this was in the aftermath of the diplomatic tensions between India and Qatar following the now-suspended Bharatiya Janata party spokesperson’s comments. Many on Twitter shared the photo with hashtags like “Qatar Exposed”.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that this banner had no connection with the recent controversy. Fans of the German football club Freiburg raised this banner before a Bundesliga match at the Europa-Park Stadion on April 02, 2022, in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany.The viral posts are archived here and here.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the photo led us to several news reports that published the photo in April this year.The Guardian used this photo on April 7 in a report on the FIFA World Cup that’s scheduled to be held in Qatar later this year. The Guardian credited the photo to Getty Images.We found the original photograph on the website of Getty Images. The caption for the photograph was taken by Matthias Hangst said, “Fans of Freiburg display a banner about boycotting the FIFA World Cup 2022 in Qatar before the Bundesliga match between Sport-Club Freiburg and FC Bayern M¼nchen at Europa-Park Stadion on April 02, 2022, in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany.”This image was also published on websites like the Middle East Monitor and Inside the Games in reports about alleged human rights violations in Qatar.Amnesty International recently released a report that has alleged human rights violations, exploitation, and deaths of migrant labourers in Qatar while working for the World Cup.The Guardian noted, “The latest Amnesty International report into private security firms who employ tens of thousands of migrant workers in Qatar is pretty damning. It says they are still subject to ‘forced labour’ and several other cases of abuse and it criticises Fifa for failing “to put in place adequate processes” to address these issues.”So, it is pretty clear that the viral banner is not about India or the fallout from rising India-Qatar tensions following Nupur Sharma’s comments. It’s about alleged human rights violations and the upcoming football world cup.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Did Moeen Ali boycott IPL over Nupur Sharma row? Unofficial Twitter account spins lie Have Nupur Sharma and Naveen Jindal’s controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad created a stir in the cricketing world as well? Several social media users claim so.A tweet supposedly from cricketer Moeen Ali has gone viral stating that the English all-rounder has demanded an apology from India following the aforementioned remarks.The tweet from the account @Moeen_Ali18 states, “If India does not apologize for its blasphemous statement, I will never go to India to play match again, I will also boycott the IPL. And I will appeal to my fellow Muslim brothers to do the same. I Love Muhammad P.B.U.H .”advertisementThe Archived versions of the Twitter account and the tweet can be seen here and here respectively.At the time of writing this, more than 13,000 people had retweeted the tweet. Others on Facebook and Twitter shared screenshots of the tweet. Archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral Tweet and the Twitter account do not belong to Moeen Ali. The English cricketer is neither active on Twitter, nor has he commented on the controversy.An impostor accountA quick look at the bio of the Twitter account in question reveals the words, “Not Official.”Further, we looked for Moeen Ali’s official Twitter account but found nothing. On Ali’s profile on the England Cricket Board's official website, all linked social media accounts were either inactive or unavailable.The Twitter account mentioned there was @MoeenAli. It had less than a hundred followers and zero tweets. It was also an unverified account.Following this, we looked for media reports on Ali’s comments on the controversy and found nothing. The cricketer recently visited India to play for Chennai Super Kings in the 15th edition of the Indian Premier League.The Bharatiya Janata Party, on June 5, suspended spokesperson Nupur Sharma and expelled Delhi media head Naveen Kumar Jindal after their controversial remarks on Prophet Mohammad that drew flak from several Muslim-majority countries.Thus, we concluded that the viral tweet was not tweeted by English cricketer Moeen Ali. It was from an unofficial account.(Written by Yash Mittal)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Salman Khurshid digs up Akhilesh era pics to bulldoze Yogi rule Bulldozers have become somewhat synonymous with strongman chief ministers following a trend of demolition drives against alleged criminals. Popularised by Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath, demolishing homes and shops of those accused of crimes has now become the modus operandi of other Bharatiya Janata Party CMs.While this method has come under criticism from civil society and opposition leaders, veteran Congress party leader Salman Khurshid’s attempt to call out the UP’s CM for this was less than successful. Sharing a series of photos of demolished buildings, Khurshid tweeted, “Not Ukraine, these are photos of Unnao and Farrukhabad of Buldozerland”.advertisementKhurshid’s tweet was retweeted by many, including Congress leader Alka Lamba. Others tweeted the photos as well, some criticising, and some praising the Yogi Adityanath government.The archived versions of such posts can be seen here, and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that three out of the four images shared by Khurshid are from former CM Akhilesh Yadav’s regime.Old pics recycledA reverse search of the first three photos led us to similar images in an Amar Ujala report from May 2016. In 2016, Akhilesh Yadav was the Chief Minister of UP. Yogi Adityanath came to power in September 2017.As per the Amar Ujala reports, these photos were from a demolition drive in Loha Mandi (iron market) and Bartan Bazar (utensils market), located between Ataullah Nala and Chhota Chauraha in Unnao. The district administration demolished around 85 supposedly illegal buildings in the area.We were unable to find a source for the fourth photo tweeted by Khurshid.What did Khurshid say?India Today contacted Khurshid and asked the veteran Congress leader about the photos. He said, “The images were shared with me by the locals of Farrukhabad where demolition is happening. At the time of tweeting the post, I was not aware the first three images were old.”Khurshid claimed that the fourth photo was from Farrukhabad. India Today has reached out to the local who shared the fourth photo with Khurshid. This story will be updated as and when we receive a response.As per reports, for the last month and a half, a demolition drive has been on in Farrukhabad. Authorities have demolished more than a dozen allegedly illegal buildings worth crores of rupees.However, it is clear that three of the four photos shared by Khurshid are indeed from 2016 and not related to the Yogi Adityanath government.Update: After getting in touch with a local, India Today was able to ascertain that the fourth photo shared by Khurshid was current. The photo showed a demolished house on Narkasa road in Kadrigate, Farrukhabad.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Cops recently lathicharged people in Kanpur, but this video is from Gorakhpur, and from 2019 Kanpur recently witnessed violence on June 3, following controversial remarks made by a former BJP spokesperson, Nupur Sharma on the Prophet Muhammad. Police resorted to lathicharge to control the crowd.Now, a video of cops lathi-charging people has gone viral. Many on Facebook shared it claiming the police lathicharge was from the recent Kanpur incident.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral video is neither recent nor from Kanpur. It is from a 2019 anti-CAA protest in Gorakhpur.advertisementThe viral posts are archived here and here.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of some keyframes of the video led us to the same video shared by the Facebook page of MMIS - Majlis E Mohammadi Islamic Samiti Official on December 20, 2019. It said the incident was in Gorakhpur.Subsequent searches led us to a video report by Live Hindustan from December 20, 2019. Per this news report, after Friday namaz, people gathered to protest against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) at Nakhash Chowk, Gorakhpur. There was stone-pelting during the protest and subsequently, the police dispersed the crowd by charging with batons and firing tear gas shells.The exact portion of the viral video can be seen after the 1.10-minute mark in the YouTube video.During the anti-CAA protests in 2019, several parts of Uttar Pradesh witnessed violence and police lathicharge. The viral video from Gorakhpur alongside other incidents from different parts of UP was also reported by The Lallantop, which can be seen here.Per reports, at least a dozen people, including two police officials were injured in the violence that broke out in Kanpur on June 3. Eighteen people have reportedly been arrested in connection with the violence.Thus, it is clear that although the UP police had resorted to lathicharge in Kanpur to control the crowd, the viral video in question has nothing to do with it. The video is from 2019 and was shot during an anti-CAA protest in Gorakhpur.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Doctored image shared to advertise BJP's 'blooming' foothold in Tamil Nadu The Tamil Nadu unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party staged a protest in Chennai against fuel price hikes on June 2. Reportedly, the event was attended by over 15,000 party cadres.Amid these developments, a post cheering for BJP workers in Tamil Nadu has gone viral on social media. "Lotus is blooming in Tamil Nadu," several users captioned a photo that showed four men hoisting the party flag, standing on each other's shoulders.advertisementThe photo was tweeted by multiple verified handles including Himachal Pradesh BJP spokesperson Prajwal Busta and former North Delhi Mayor Ravinder Gupta.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the viral image was doctored. In the viral photo, BJP’s flag replaced the Bahujan Samaj Party flag.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the image showed a handful of results. The top result was a May 31 tweet from the account of Shirisha Swaero Akinapally, the spokesperson of the BSP's Telangana unit. However, in this photo, the men were seen hoisting a BSP flag."Our brothers and sisters climbed the ladder and hoisted the blue flag at the heartbeat of the masses. Millions of such youths are following in the footsteps of @RSPraveenSwaerofor the establishment of a Bahujan Rajya Sabha in Telangana," Akinapally wrote in Telugu. It was retweeted by many, including BSP Telangana state coordinator RS Praveen Kumar.We also found the photo with the BSP flag uploaded on a Pinterest page called "Ambedkari Status".We ran the two images on the image error analysis platforms Forensically and FotoForensics. When an image is examined under Error Level Analysis on these websites, altered or appended parts stand out in colour grade from the rest of the image.While there were no evident mismatches on the BSP image, the orange portion of the BJP flag stood out on the FotoForensics test.Similarly, the BJP flag appears glared out compared to the rest of the image's scale on Forensically as well. This can be seen below.Thus, we concluded that the photo used of the BJP flag was a doctored one. The original photo had a BSP flag.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Shocking CCTV footage of brutal public murder in Delhi’s Azadpur shared with false Rohingya spin A shocking video has gone viral with the claim that it captured communal violence in broad daylight.In the CCTV footage, two men could be seen attacking a man even as a crowd was present. One onlooker attempted to stop the assault. However, one of the assailants hit the victim’s head with rocks and stabs him several times. Following that, he also appeared to slit the victim’s throat.advertisementThose sharing this graphic video claimed that the assailants were Rohingya Muslims and the victim was a Hindu man.here and here. Other similar claims can be seenandThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral video is from Delhi’s Azadpur and has no communal angle to it. Both the victim and the culprits are Hindu.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the keyframes of the video led us to several news reports related to the incident. An India Today report stated that the incident occurred in the afternoon of June 3 in New Delhi’s Azadpur.According to the report, a quarrel broke out after Narender, the victim, repeatedly approached Rahul Kali to borrow money to buy drugs. Per the police, an annoyed Rahul called his brother Rohit Kali to Mandir Wali Gali in Azadpur. The duo then brutally attacked Narender.Following the attack, Narender was rushed to the BJRM hospital for treatment. Later, he was referred to a higher centre where he was declared brought dead.The Indian Express quoted the DCP of Northwest Delhi Usha Rangnani saying, “The accused brothers, Rahul and Rohit Kali, have been arrested. The victim, Narender alias Bunti, and Rahul were previously involved in cases of robbery and snatching.” An FIR has reportedly been filed under IPC sections 302 (murder) and 34 (common intention).To verify if Rohit and Rahul Kali were Rohingya Muslims, India Today contacted the Adarsh Nagar Police Station, under which Azadpur falls. Inspector Rajendra there confirmed that the incident was not communal and everyone involved — Rohit Kali, Rahul Kali, and Narender — is Hindu.Thus, we conclude that the incident in the viral video was not communal. Rohit and Rahul Kali, the brothers who brutally killed Narender, are not Rohingya Muslims; they are Hindus.(Written by Yash Mittal)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: 2021 prayer service for Pak politician viral as mass gathering against Nupur Sharma’s comments Amid international backlash following Nupur Sharma’s controversial remarks on Prophet Muhammad during a primetime television news debate, a video of a massive gathering went viral. Those sharing this clip claimed it was from a protest against the former BJP spokesperson.The video was shared with hashtags like #OurProphetOurHonour and captions in Hindi that read, "For the sake of Prophet Muhammad, people of Saudi Arabia, Iran, Qatar, Kuwait, Libia, Oman, Bahrain, and Afghanistan have come together."advertisementArchived versions of some similar claims can be seen here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found these posts to be misleading and have nothing to do with the ongoing row. The video is more than a year old and is from Lahore, Pakistan.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the screenshots from the viral clip led us to the same video uploaded to YouTube on January 4, 2021. A channel named “Labbaik News” from Pakistan shared it with the title: "Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi Chehlum | TLP Chehlum 2021."found a tweet from January 3, 2021, that contained the same video. The text in Urdu claimed this gathering was "spiritual scenes of Chehlum of Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi." We alsofrom January 3, 2021, that contained the same video. The text in Urdu claimed this gathering was "spiritual scenes of Chehlum of Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi."Subsequent searches led us to a report on a Pakistani website published on January 3, 2021. It noted that thousands of people attended the Chehlum — a remembrance and prayer service on or about the fortieth day after death — for Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi. He was the founder of Tehreek-e-Labbaik, a far-right political party in Pakistan. On November 19, 2020, Rizvi died at the age of 54.photography website Shutterstock. The caption stated: “Large numbers activists of hardline religious political party Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP) shouting slogans during participation in the 40th day prayer of late Khadim Hussain Rizvi at Multan Road in Lahore on January 03, 2021." We searched for photographs of the event and found one on the stick image andThe caption stated: “Large numbers activists of hardline religious political party Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP) shouting slogans during participation in the 40th day prayer of late Khadim Hussain Rizvi at Multan Road in Lahore on January 03, 2021."When we compared the Shutterstock photo with the screenshot of the viral video, similar-looking advertising boards, buildings, and the elevated metro track made it clear that the gathering seen in the viral was indeed held on January 3, 2021, in Lahore, Pakistan.Qatar, Iran, Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia condemned Sharma’s controversial remarks and called for "respect for all beliefs and religions." Protests against Sharma have also taken place across India. But this video clearly does not show a mass gathering to register a protest against the now-suspended BJP spokesperson. In fact, this video is more than a year old and is from Pakistan.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Definitely not Tamil Nadu! This video of people driving over the Indian flag is from Karachi Among the more bizarre sights on the internet this week was a video of a bunch of cars driving over the Indian flag taped to the road, all the while cheered by people carrying Pakistan’s flag.Bizarre as the sight was, the claim alongside it was questionable. Those sharing the video said this scene was from Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the video in question was not from Tamil Nadu, but from Karachi, Pakistan.Geolocating the videoAs mentioned earlier, one can see many people holding the Pakistani flag in this video. At three minutes 38 seconds of the video, we noticed a white van with “The Hunar Foundation ” written on it.According to the website of The Hunar Foundation, the organisation is based out of Karachi and focuses on providing technical training in Pakistan.This indicated that the video was likely from Pakistan. There were other such clues. For example, the rickshaws seen in the video do not look similar to the ones seen on the Tamil Nadu roads.We also noticed in the video that most four-wheelers had yellow licence plates. Karachi-based journalist Tauseef Razi Mallick told India Today that in Pakistan, yellow licence plates were found in the Sindh province, whose capital is Karachi.At the start of the video, we noticed the signboard of a shop with “Sanam'' written on it. When we searched for shops named Sanam in Karachi, we came across a “Sanam Boutique” whose font and design looked similar to the one in the video. According to this site, the boutique is located in Tariq Road, Delhi Mercantile Society in Karachi.YouTube video of Tariq Road in Karachi, we came across the same Sanam Boutique as seen in the viral clip. In a 2017in Karachi, we came across the same Sanam Boutique as seen in the viral clip.The Google Maps Street View of Tariq Road can be seen below.Is this video from a recent protest?We found that the same video or screenshots from it have been in circulation on the internet since at least March 2020. In the video, a number of people can be seen wearing masks. This indicates that the video is likely not from before the Covid-19 pandemic.So, while we weren’t able to pinpoint the date of the video or why this event took place, we could say with certainty that this video was from Karachi, Pakistan — not Tamil Nadu.
label: truth

content: Fact Check video: Scene from web series shared as murder of Sidhu Moose Wala It was reported that 30 empty bullet shells were recovered from the crime scene where Punjabi singer and Congress leader Sidhu Moose Wala was shot dead by unidentified assailants on May 29. Several days after the murder at Jawaharke village in Mansa, the investigators are yet to zero in on the assailants.Meanwhile, a video has gone viral on social media with the claim that it showed the ambush by the killers on Moose Wala. "Waheguru ji, see how the killers of Moose Wala attacked him," the translation of a Punjabi Facebook post that shared the video read.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. The footage isn't real but clipped from an action series streaming online.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Drone strike from Azeri-Armenian war viral as Ukrainian attack on Russian tanks As per the latest reports, Russia has intensified shelling in the Sievierodonetsk and Lysychansk regions as Ukrainian forces refuse to give in. As the conflict thus drags on with no visible sign of peace, a video has gone viral on social media with the claim that it shows a successful Ukrainian drone strike on Russian tanks."Ukraine's armed forces show a video with a Bayraktar drone destroying Russian tanks," wrote a Facebook user while sharing it.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. The footage is not from the Ukraine-Russian war. It was shot in 2020 when Armenia and Azerbaijan clashed for the control of the Nagorno-Karabakh region.AFWA ProbeThe claim names Bayraktar drones responsible for neutralising enemy ground units. Forbes calls Turkish-made Bayraktar TB2 "the most celebrated drone of the age."Known for its armour-breaching capacity, Ukraine’s original fleet of drones was estimated to be 36 strong. There are reports of replacements still reaching Ukraine as many of these have been lost in the course of the war.Where is the video from?A reverse search of the video's keyframes on Yandex returned results in plenty — most dating back to 2020. Among the top results was an Instagram post from a verified account of noted Russian TV journalist Olga Skabeyeva.On September 28, 2020, Skabeyeva shared the same video, writing, "Azerbaijani video with an Armenian tank. The hope that by morning they would change their minds did not come true."This confirmed that the video is not recently shot from Ukraine as claimed in the viral post.Yandex also led us to a handful of YouTube videos that were uploaded in September 2020. Like Skabeyeva’s post, they claimed it showed Azerbaijan on the offence against Armenian troops. Some of these videos can be seen below.Azerbaijan and Armenia fought over the control of long-disputed Nagorno-Karabakh territory from September to November 2020. Supported by Turkey, Azerbaijan made major breakthroughs before a ceasefire came into force.We checked for more evidence to assert that the viral video was from the war in 2020. We found a photo story on the Karabakh conflict in a Turkish news portal. It explained how Turkish-made Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) helped Azerbaijan edge out its foe on the battlefield. The story contained many visuals of destroyed tanks that looked similar to the scenes from the viral video.Similarly, another website called “sonhaberler.com” in September 2020 used a screenshot from the viral video to report the total damage suffered by Armenia in the conflict.India Today has earlier debunked claims that linked unrelated visuals to the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.Hence, we concluded that the video of a lethal drone strike shared as a Ukrainian offence against Russia was shot almost two years ago when Armenia fought Azerbaijan.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Did a Hindu family in US convert to Islam? 2015 photo of German family shared with false spin A Hindu family of four in the US converted to Islam. Well, at least that is what a viral photo claims.Many on Facebook shared a photo of four people — an adult man and an adult woman, and a boy and a girl. The photo also contained text that said that these four supposedly Hindu people in the US embraced Islam.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War room (AWFA) found that the viral image is seven years old and from Egypt. It shows a German family that converted to Islam.The viral posts are archived here and here.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the photo led us to an old news report that had published the viral photo along with other photos of the same family.This article was published on the Egyptian news portal youm7.com on November 6, 2015.According to this article, a German family had converted to Islam at the Al-Tawhid mosque in Hurghada City, Egypt on November 6, 2015. As seen in the viral photo, the German man, Donel Klaus, his wife, and their children were welcomed by the Imam of the mosque. Each family member was gifted a copy of the Quran.The images were also posted on a Facebook page called “Muslim Players” on November 7, 2015, with the caption: “The German Donel Klaus and his family reverted to Islam today at Hurghada, Egypt. They entered Masjid At-Tawheed and asked for the Imam to declare shahada. Masha Allah!! Congratulations and welcome to your big family.”Another youm7.com report on from November 7, 2015, gave details about how many foreigners converted to Islam on November 6, at the various mosques of the Egyptian city of Hurghada. It also mentioned the conversion of the Donel Klaus family.We could not find any credible news report confirming any religious conversion of a Hindu family to Islam in the US recently. Thus, we concluded that an old photo of a German family that converted to Islam in Egypt was shared with a false spin.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Now, shootout scene from web series shared as murder of Sidhu Moose Wala It was reported that 30 empty bullet shells were recovered from the crime scene where Punjabi singer and Congress leader Sidhu Moose Wala was shot dead by unidentified assailants on May 29. Several days after the murder at Jawaharke village in Mansa, the investigators are yet to zero in on the assailants.Meanwhile, a video has gone viral on social media with the claim that it showed the ambush by the killers on Moose Wala. "Waheguru ji, see how the killers of Moose Wala attacked him," the translation of a Punjabi Facebook post that shared the video read.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. The footage isn't real but clipped from an action series streaming online.AFWA ProbeWhen the keyframes of the video were reverse searched on Google, several YouTube videos were found.The top result, uploaded on August 31, 2021, was titled "Gangster gun fire attitude WhatsApp status."Another user, who had uploaded the video on May 27, 2021, had said it showed an attack on Neeraj Bawana. Neeraj is a notorious gangster who is serving his term in the Tihar jail and allegedly has networks across Delhi, Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan.This confirmed that the video is not the footage of the fatal ambush on the murdered singer and politician as it is available online for over a year now.While the visuals looked very dramatic to be original, the search showed no hints to locate its origin. We chose to check the comments below all YouTube links that featured the clip. In this way, it was found a person had mentioned the name of the web series "Shukla The Tiger" as a comment to the video on a channel called "WhatsApp Status".When checked, it was found that "Shukla The Tiger" is a Hindi action web series streaming on MX Player since 2021. As the artist from the trailer looked similar to the man in the viral video, we checked the web series.Six minutes into the eighth episode of the series named "Ek Dhokha", a shootout erupts between two rival groups. We noticed that the Bolero SUV and the dress of the men seen firing at the rivals are the same as that in the video. A comparison can be seen below.This helped us confirm that the viral video being shared as the attack on slain singer-politician Sidhu Moose Wala is not real. It is a scene from a web series called "Shukla The Tiger".(With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Sonia Gandhi's 7-year-old comment goes viral as response to fresh ED summons The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned Congress president Sonia Gandhi and MP Rahul Gandhi to appear before it on June 8 in connection with the National Herald money laundering case.Amid this development, a video clip has gone viral on social media as the Congress leader's reaction to the ED's move. “I am the daughter-in-law of Indira Gandhi. I am not scared of anyone”, Sonia Gandhi is heard saying in Hindi in the video.advertisementMultiple Facebook users have posted this video clip alongside a Hindi caption that translates to, “When the police come to catch a loafer who steals in the streets, he says that my uncle is an MLA or minister. Just like that, when the ED calls Sonia for interrogation on stealing from the government treasury, Sonia says, I am Indra's daughter-in-law”.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that while the ED has summoned Sonia and Rahul Gandhi, this viral video is from 2015. It shows what Sonia Gandhi had said after a Delhi court asked them to appear in the National Herald case.The viral posts are saved here and here.AFWA probeRelevant searches using keywords on Google led us to several articles and news clips published by the mainstream media in 2015. A news bulletin uploaded on the YouTube channel of India Today in December 2015 showed the exact reaction of Sonia Gandhi that has gone viral now.The same video was uploaded on the news portal of “The Hindu” around the same time.“NDTV” and “The Times Of India” had also published news reports on Sonia Gandhi’s comments.Per these reports, Sonia Gandhi had said this in 2015 after a trial court in Delhi asked her and Rahul Gandhi, along with five others to appear in the National Herald case. The petitioner Subramanian Swamy had accused the Congress leaders of cheating in court.Hence, it is clear that Sonia Gandhi’s comment about being Indira Gandhi's daughter-in-law was not made recently after being summoned by the ED. The viral clip is seven years old.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check video: No, Hardik Patel wasn't slapped after joining BJP A video of Hardik Patel has gone viral on social media with the claim that he was 'welcomed' into the BJP with a slap.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. This video shows Hardik Patel getting slapped more than three years ago when he was still with the Congress party.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Huge crowd at jawan’s funeral in Gujarat shared as Sidhu Moose Wala’s last rites This special report takes viewers onto the sets of the upcoming Tamil movie 'Parashakti', starring Shiva Karthikeyan, Ravi, and Sri Leela. The film is meticulously recreating the era of the 1950s and 1960s in Tamil Nadu, focusing on a pivotal moment in the state's history. The central theme appears to be the anti-Hindi agitation, as the report highlights props and set pieces depicting student protests and the political climate that led to the rise of the Dravidian government. The report notes that 'this movie is expected to touch the part because that anti-Hindi agitation paved the way for the Dravidian government'. Viewers get a glimpse of nostalgic elements from the period, including Goli Soda bottles, pull rickshaws, a vintage Chevrolet, and recreations of old railway and radio stations, all contributing to the historical setting of the film which is expected to release on Pongal 2026.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: This viral video does not show midnight police action against Kanpur "rioters" Kanpur witnessed incidents of stone-pelting and violence on June 3, Friday. As per reports, 36 people have been arrested and 1,000 others listed as unknown accused on charges of rioting and attempt to murder. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed the police to identify those responsible and take strict action.There are several videos of police action on the alleged rioters doing the rounds on social media. Among these is a video that shows policemen thrashing a few men on the street at night.advertisementMultiple verified Twitter handles and Facebook users have posted this viral video alongside a Hindi caption that translates to, "These strange sounds coming from the streets of Kanpur at midnight have been called auspicious in the scriptures. Babaji's police taking good care of Jihadi stone pelters."India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the viral video is neither recent nor from Kanpur. This 2020 video was from the Mumbra area of Thane in Maharashtra.The viral posts are saved here, here and here.AFWA probeA reverse image search of the viral video's keyframes gave us clues that this video had circulated earlier on the internet, besides multiple claims.While some netizens had claimed the video was from Indore during the days of Covid lockdown, some others claimed that it was from Telangana. Several users raised doubts over these viral claims and said the video was from Mumbra, Thane.Taking this as a clue, we ran a keyword search accordingly in Hindi and found multiple news reports published on Hindi news portals which had reported the real story of the video.A YouTube news channel, "Hindustani Reporter," had uploaded a news clip along with the same viral video to report an incident on March 29, 2020. As per this report, the incident happened on March 27, 2020, in Kausa, Shree Lanka area of Mumbra, when supporters of two local politicians clashed. The police resorted to a lathi-charge to disperse the mob and regain control of the situation.Thus, it is clear that a two-year-old video from Maharashtra is being circulated with the misleading claim that it shows police action in Kanpur after the recent Friday violence.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Youth who got away injured after water park accident "killed" by netizens! Amusement parks are supposed to give visitors a happy time. People buy tickets hoping to have fun and leave with memories to cherish. It is the last place one would expect tragedy to strike.If a video circulating on social media is to be believed, that is exactly what happened to a youth who was fatally injured following an accident at Kanpur's Blue World Theme Park. The footage shows a young man dropping unconscious in a pool after colliding with a woman who came sliding into the water. Blood is seen gushing out from his head as his friends carry him off.advertisement"A woman sliding in the Blue Word theme park collides with a young man. The youth died on the spot due to the collision. The video of the death went viral. Wherever it is from, this incident should not be seen from the point of view of news. The lesson that can be learnt from this incident is that we and our family should be very serious and careful while having fun in the water park. There should never be any carelessness in the swimming pool," a Facebook post alongside the video read.Similar claims have been archived here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. The video shows an accident that happened at Mukundra water park in Rajasthan. The injured person didn't die but was let go after undergoing treatment for his head injury.AFWA ProbeDespite multiple efforts, we couldn't retrieve any reports of accidental death at amusement parks in Kanpur or anywhere else in recent times. However, when we looked for accidents and head injuries caused at water parks, there were a few articles available. Among these was a report by Aajtak published on June 3, 2022.The report said that a man was hurt at Mukundra park on Kota Road of Rajasthan's Jhalawar district. While the video has gone viral on social media, the injured youth is undergoing treatment at SRG Hospital, the story said. From the screengrabs attached alongside the report, it became clear that it was the same incident from the viral video.Following this clue, we looked up the Mukundra water park in Jhalawar. Ran by the Mukundra Hotels & Resorts, Google Maps had several photos of the park. We found the pool and the twin spiral water slides similar to those in the video in these images.Meanwhile, a similar search on Blue World Theme Park showed the structure and colour scheme of the water slides here are different to those seen in the video.For further clarity, we reached out to stringer Firoz Ahmed, who compiled the report for AajTak. He confirmed that the video is from Rajasthan and not Uttar Pradesh. For further clarity, we reached out to stringer Firoz Ahmed, who compiled the report for AajTak. He confirmed that the video is from Rajasthan and not Uttar Pradesh."It happened on May 28, 2022. The victim belongs to Kota's Ramganj Mandi. He was rushed to the Emergency OT at Jhalawar's SRG Hospital where he got 3 stitches for the wound. He was later discharged," Firoz said. No police report was filed and the woman involved in the accident belonged to the same group as the victim, he added.Firoz shared more photos and videos from the accident spot that helped us confirm that it happened at Mukundra water park in Rajasthan.Hence, it is clear that a man didn't collapse and die in Kanpur's Blue World Theme Park following a mishap as claimed in the post. The footage shows a minor accident that happened in Jhalawar, Rajasthan.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in New Delhi and Firoz Ahmed in Rajasthan)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Hardik Patel did not get slapped after joining BJP, viral video is from 2019 Days after quitting the Congress, Gujarat Patidar leader Hardik Patel joined the ranks of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Thursday. Meanwhile, a video of the new recruit in the saffron camp has gone viral on social media with the claim that he was 'welcomed' with a slap.In the seven-second-long muted video, Patel is slapped by a man while speaking from a stage.advertisementUsers have shared this video alongside a caption in Hindi that translates to, "Warm welcome and greeting to Hardik Patel as soon as he joins BJP."Archived versions of similar claims can be seen here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. This video shows Hardik Patel getting slapped more than three years ago when he was still with the Congress party.AFWA ProbeA keyword search on Google showed multiple news reports published in April 2019 -- suggesting that the incident is not recent.An article in 'The Economic Times' from April 19, 2019, noted that Patel was delivering his speech at Gujarat's Surendranagar district for the Lok Sabha elections when he was slapped by an unidentified man.As the logo of 'Hindustan Times' was visible in the viral video, we searched for the original one and found it uploaded on April 19. We found the now viral part 12 seconds into this original version.According to a report published in India Today, the man who slapped Patel was later identified as Tarun Gajjar. It also noted that Gajjar had some personal grudge against the Patidar leader and hence slapped him.Hardik Patel, the young face of the Patidar caste of Gujarat, made his political debut with Congress in 2019. Now, his move to the BJP months before the state assembly polls has further dented the aspirations of the Congress party to seize power in the saffron fort.Thus, it is safe to conclude that the video of Hardik Patel getting slapped was not shot after he joined the BJP but from 2019 when he was a member of Congress.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: The pied piper of Bangladesh: A curious story of a honey collector A video on social media has been making the rounds with the claim that a modern-day devout Hindu man allegedly has the power to sway honey bees through his flute.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the man in this video is Mehtab Morol, a Muslim honey collector from Jessore, Bangladesh.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: A different Jama Masjid! This photo of a damaged dome is from a UP mosque, not Delhi Heavy rains and hailstorm in Delhi on May 30 were a respite to the sweltering heat, but they came at a cost. The historic Jama Masjid suffered damage that included the finial of the main dome getting dislodged.The incident was widely reported and following it, a photo of a dislodged dome was circulated on social media with the claim that it showed the damaged Jama Masjid dome. One such post can be seen below.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the photo in question is not from Delhi. It was taken in 2017 in Uttar Pradesh.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the viral image led us to several media reports from October 2017 that carried the same photograph. According to a Patrika report from October 21, 2017, the photo showed an old Jama Masjid at Uparkot in UP's Bulandshahr. One of the three domes of the mosque had collapsed during the afternoon prayers, injuring three children and a dozen of adults. One of the children succumbed to injuries on the way to the hospital.A video report about the incident was published by News18 on October 24, 2017. The photo that is now in circulation is a screenshot from this video report.Following the damage caused by Monday’s storm in Delhi, the Shahi Imam of the Jama Masjid wrote to the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) requesting removal of the dangling part of the crown and repair of the ornamental structure.In the letter to ASI's Director General V Vidtavathi, Jama Masjid Shahi Imam Syed Ahmed Bukhari mentioned that after being broken into multiple pieces in the storm, some parts fell on the terrace below the main dome, and one very heavy part is "still hanging precariously from the dome and it may fall any time".It is thus clear that the viral image in question is from a 2017 incident in Uttar Pradesh and is not related to Delhi’s Jama Masjid getting damaged in a storm.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Underwater tunnel from Europe shared as proposed Brahmaputra river project in Assam A high-speed train emerges from a tunnel. Adjacent to it, heavy vehicles speed past on busy roads. What appears to be an ordinary sight is made special because of its physical location — underneath a mighty tempestuous river.This is what the proposed underwater tunnel being built under the Brahmaputra river in Assam is projected to look like, or at least that’s what a viral photo on social media claims.advertisement"Underwater road and railway line, this is said to be a 14 km long tunnel built under the Brahmaputra river in Assam. This is the new India," a tweet that carried the photo boasts.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. This was a graphical depiction of the Fehmarn Belt Fixed Link or the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel, an immersed tunnel system that will link the German island of Fehmarn with the Danish island of Lolland. The tunnel system is still under construction.A plan is in placeIndia’s first underwater road-rail tunnel is set to be built across the Brahmaputra. According to news reports, the Rs 7,000 crore project is the brainchild of the Railway Ministry, the Road Transport Ministry and the Border Road Organisation (BRO). A first of its kind in India, the tunnel will be 9.8 kilometres long and serve both civilian and strategic purposes, a May report in The Federal said.A Times of India report said the proposed project will contain three parallel tunnels — one for road, another for rail, and the third one for emergency use. It will be constructed using tunnel boring machines and may take in excess of two years to complete.So, the tunnel project is real. But is the photo that’s being shared showing the same project?But does it look like this?A reverse search of the photo returned results in plenty. The website for World Highways magazine used the photo in a June 2017 report on the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel — an underwater tunnel between Denmark and Germany that’s still under work. Built under the European Union’s Trans European Network (TEN-T) programme, the 18 km-long immersed tunnel combined road and rail link connecting the Baltic Sea regions of Germany and Denmark, the report said.A website called TricksFast also used the same image in a July 2021 article about the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel.The photo was also used on the first page of a document by an organisation called Tunnel Engineering Consultants (TEC) that called Fehmarnbelt "the world's longest immersed tunnel."More details of the ambitious project can be seen in the video below.advertisementIndia Today has debunked similar claims before that wrongly attributed European tunnels to upcoming projects from other parts of the world.Thus, we concluded that while a tunnel system under the Brahmaputra river in Assam has been proposed, the photo shared has nothing to do with it — it is of a European tunnel that’s still under construction.(With inputs from Adarsh Singh in New Delhi)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Kerala has many Messi fans but this old video does not show celebration of Argentina's La Finalissima 2022 win Lionel Messi stole the show in front of a packed crowd at the Wembley Stadium as Argentina's national football team celebrated a 3-0 victory over Italy to claim La Finalissima 2022. Following this, a video went viral on social media claiming it showed the legendary Indian fans in Kerala celebrating Argentina's victory.The video showed a bike rally with men carrying Argentina’s flag, hooting and cheering as they sped on a road. A Twitter user shared the video with the claim, “My town in India celebrating Argentina’s win today. We love Messi”.advertisementThe archived version of this post can be seen here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that though the video was from the Indian state of Kerala, it was almost a year old. Obviously, it has no connection with Argentina’s victory in La Finalissima 2022.AFWA ProbeThe devil is in the detailIn the viral video, several people could be seen wearing masks, indicating that it was likely shot in 2020 or 2021 when Covid-19 masking rules were stricter. When we reverse-searched frames from the video, we found that many people had shared it in 2021.The bikes could be seen crossing a bridge located near a beach. An abundance of palm trees also suggested that it was shot in a coastal area.We were able to spot two bike number registration plates- ‘KL11B’ and ‘KL10P’. While the RTO code ‘KL11’ is registered under Kozhikode, Kerala. ‘KL10’ is registered under Kerala’s Malappuram.Both districts are located in the Northern part of Kerala, indicating that this video could have been shot somewhere in that region.What did a Keralite Messi fan say?We found a video of a similar bike rally by Messi fans in India that was shared by ESPN Argentina’s Twitter account on July 11, 2021.ESPN credited the video to someone called KM Sudhi from Kerala. Sudhi is a member of the Kerala Youth Congress. India Today reached out to Sudhi, who told us that the viral video in question was indeed from Kerala.Sudhi confirmed to us that his friend had sent this video to him. “This video was shot in Kerala after Messi-led Argentina won the Copa America title in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on July 11, 2021,” Sudhi said, adding he too was a massive fan of Messi.We also found multiple media reports stating how the soccer fans in Kerala celebrated Argentina’s Copa America victory in July 2021 with bike rallies.Thus, we concluded that last year’s video of Lionel Messi fans in Kerala celebrating Argentina’s Copa America win was shared as fans’ reaction to the team’s La Finalissima 2022 victory.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena)
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Video of Virat Kohli batting left-handed for RCB isn't real This special report takes viewers onto the sets of the upcoming Tamil movie 'Parashakti', starring Shiva Karthikeyan, Ravi, and Sri Leela. The film is meticulously recreating the era of the 1950s and 1960s in Tamil Nadu, focusing on a pivotal moment in the state's history. The central theme appears to be the anti-Hindi agitation, as the report highlights props and set pieces depicting student protests and the political climate that led to the rise of the Dravidian government. The report notes that 'this movie is expected to touch the part because that anti-Hindi agitation paved the way for the Dravidian government'. Viewers get a glimpse of nostalgic elements from the period, including Goli Soda bottles, pull rickshaws, a vintage Chevrolet, and recreations of old railway and radio stations, all contributing to the historical setting of the film which is expected to release on Pongal 2026.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Kareena Kapoor did not ask people to not watch 'Laal Singh Chaddha', 2020 video shared with false spin The buzz around Aamir Khan’s highly-anticipated upcoming movie “Laal Singh Chaddha”, a remake of Tom Hanks' Hollywood hit “Forrest Gump”, has been loud on social media. However, amid the memes and discussions, a video that features Khan’s co-star Kareena Kapoor Khan has gone viral with a startling claim.Those sharing the video claimed that Kapoor appealed to people to boycott “Laal Singh Chaddha”. It was also shared along with the hashtag #BoycottLaalSinghChaddha.advertisementIn the viral video, she could be heard saying, “The audience has made us, no one else has made us. The same people pointing fingers are the ones who have made these nepotistic stars right? Aap jaa re ho na film dekhne? Mat jao (You’re going to theatres to watch the film? Don’t go). Nobody has forced you. So I don’t understand it. I find this whole discussion is completely weird.”The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral clip was taken from a 2020 news debate and it has no connection with “Laal Singh Chaddha”. Kapoor was responding to a question about nepotism in Bollywood.The viral posts are saved here and here.AFWA ProbeA simple reverse search of frames from the viral video led us to an August 2020 report in Pinkvilla. It quoted the same response from Kapoor that had gone viral in an interview about nepotism in Bollywood.Another report in India Times around the same time mentioned this interview was given to journalist Barkha Dutt for “We The Women”.We then found the longer version of the interview on the YouTube channel of Mojo Story, a news outlet led by Dutt. The title of the YouTube video was, “Kareena Kapoor has been called the Ultimate Insider. This is what she says on the Nepotism Debate”.Around the 3.35 mark in the video, Dutt asks Kapoor, “The way I see it, Kareena you will definitely get an easier start, you will definitely get more doors to open, but if the audience doesn’t like you there’s nothing you can do about it.” Kapoor’s response was the section seen in the viral clip.So, it is clear that in this video from 2020, what Kareena Kapoor said was in the context of nepotism in Bollywood. It has nothing to do with “Laal Singh Chaddha”.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Freedom fighter’s pic shared as fictitious Assamese revolutionary along with an unverifiable anecdote On social media, people have been sharing the photo of an elderly woman claiming she is Kamaladevi Hazarika, a revolutionary from Assam who gave a befitting reply to a pastor who tried to proselytise her and her family to Christianity.In a nutshell, the story people shared alongside the photo was as follows: A pastor named Cruz was sent to Assam to promote Christianity. There, he was employed by a prestigious family to teach English to a boy. Soon, the pastor realised that the boy's grandmother was the most influential person in the family, and if he was able to convert her to Christianity, the whole family would follow suit.advertisementThe pastor then began telling the grandmother stories of how Jesus Christ cured leprosy, gave sight to the blind, etc. The grandmother, however, said that this was nothing compared to the miracles of Lord Rama and Lord Krishna. Despite this, the pastor did not lose hope.One day, he brought a cake from the church and offered it to the old lady. As soon as she consumed it, the pastor exclaimed that because she had eaten a church offering, she was now Christian. The grandmother boxed the pastor’s ear and told him that, by his logic, him eating at her place every day, breathing the air and drinking the water in the land of Hinduism meant he was now Hindu.Many shared this story. Similar posts can be seen here, here, and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the woman seen in the photo was Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, a well-known freedom fighter and social reformer from Mangalore, Karnataka. At the same time, there are no historical records of any revolutionary named Kamaladevi Hazarika hailing from Assam.AFWA ProbeWe could not find any evidence about a popular revolutionary from Assam called Kamaladevi Hazarika. Even searches in multiple languages did not yield any results.However, we did find that the same story has been circulating online since at least 2017.What’s noteworthy is that according to CrowdTangle, a social media analysis tool, this story was posted more than 100 times on Facebook in the past week and garnered nearly 31,000 interactions at the time of writing this story.Who is the lady in the photo?A reverse search of the viral photo led us to the website of the Centre For Cultural Resources And Training, an autonomous Indian organisation under the aegis of the Ministry of Culture. The site stated that this was the photo of Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, a notable social reformer, freedom fighter, and art enthusiast. It also stated that CCRT was also pioneered by Chattopadhyay.advertisementChattopadhyay received multiple awards in recognition of her public service, like the Padma Bhushan, the Padma Vibhushan, the Ramon Magsaysay Award, and the UNESCO Award. She died in Mumbai on October 29, 1988, at the age of 85.Chattopadhyay’s biography, “Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay Portrait of a rebel”, written by Jamila Brijbhushan, is available on the Wayback Machine. Using keyword search, we tried finding if there was any mention of a pastor named Cruz in it. The search did not yield any results.Her biographer speaksWe sent the viral claim to Sakuntala Narasimhan, the author of another Chattopadhyay biography called “Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay: The Romantic Rebel”. Narasimhan told India Today that Chattopadhyay did not have any such encounter in her lifetime. “I have met Kamaladevi, and spent a lot of time with her before writing my book on her. I have never heard of this story about the Christian pastor Cruz,” she said.We also asked Narasimhan if Chattopadhyay had any Assamese link, to which she said, “As far as I know, she had no Assamese connection. I have also spoken to some of her former co-workers and freedom fighters but have never heard of any of her connections to Assam.”To sum it up, freedom fighter Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay’s photo was shared by many on social media with the claim that she was Kamaladevi Hazarika, a supposed Assamese revolutionary. We found no records of Hazarika. We were also unable to ascertain the veracity of the story that has been online since at least 2017.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Yes, Bhagwant Mann took a photo with a Goldy Brar, but this wasn’t Sidhu Moose Wala’s alleged murderer The name Goldy Brar has been all over social media following the assassination of Punjabi singer Shubhdeep Singh Sidhu, known popularly as Sidhu Moose Wala. Brar, along with others, has allegedly claimed responsibility for the murder.The Punjabi singer and Congress leader’s death followed the Punjab Police withdrawing security for 424 people, including him. Following Moose Wala’s death, the Punjab government faced harsh criticism. Amid the online hullabaloo, a photo of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and another man went viral with a string of questionable claims.advertisementThe photo was a screengrab of a Facebook post made by a man called Goldy Brar on March 10. Standing alongside him in a photo was the Punjab CM. The caption said, "Congratulations CM saab.”This screengrab was shared with a wild claim. It said, “Sidhu Moosewala’s murder conspirator gangster Goldy Brar is in Canada. Canada is home to Khalistanis. Bhagwant Mann govt removed Sidhu’s security yesterday. Sidhu is killed today. Connect the dots What is the connection between Canada based Goldy Brar who is taking credit for the assassination of Moose Wala and Punjab CM Mann? Below is the picture of the two.”Similar posts can be seen here, here, and here.Did Mann really meet the man who allegedly murdered the Punjabi singer and political rival? And did the two pose for a photo after Mann was elected to the Chief Minister’s office?India Today Anti Fake News War Room’s (AFWA) investigation found that the photo was real, and the man standing with Mann is indeed called Goldy Brar. However, he is not the gangster suspected to be involved in Moose Wala’s murder.READ MORE: Fact Check: Far from his last, this Sidhu Moose Wala interview with Sonam Bajwa is more than a year oldThe namesakeA reverse search of the photo led us to the Facebook profile of Goldy Brar. On March 10, the day the Aam Aadmi Party won 92 of Punjab’s 117 assembly constituencies, Brar shared his photo with Mann.On his Facebook profile, we found another video from May 29, the day Moose Wala was assassinated. It was captioned in Punjabi, “I am Goldy Brar, son of Rajinder Singh, resident of village Jandwala. My picture is being misused on social media after today's tragic incident, the murder of Sidhu Moose Wala. I will take legal action against those people.”In the video, he appealed to the Punjab government to take action against those spreading misinformation about his involvement with Moose Wala’s assassination.To further clarify the matter, India Today got in touch with Brar, a farmer from the Fazilka district in Punjab. He said that he had no connection with the man allegedly involved in Moose Wala’s murder — except for his name.advertisementSpeaking about the photo, Brar said that he volunteered for the AAP during its 2022 Punjab assembly polls campaign. He said that he met Mann at Mohali in January and that’s where the two posed for the photo. Following the AAP’s historic victory in Punjab, he shared the photo on Facebook.The other GoldyAs per reports, Punjab Police said that aside from Brar, gangster Lawrence Bishnoi was involved in the killing. Lucky, a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, has taken responsibility from Canada.Goldy Brar, whose real name is Satwinderjit Singh, is known to be a close aide of Bishnoi. Based in Canada, Brar is wanted in the 2021 murder of Faridkot District Youth Congress president Gurlal Singh Pehlwan. Reportedly , a total of 16 criminal cases have been registered against Brar in Punjab — he has been acquitted in four cases.In connection to Moose Wala's murder, a Facebook post supposedly made by Brar said , "I, along with Sachin Bishnoi Dhattaranwali, Lawrence Bishnoi group, take responsibility for the killing of Sidhu Moose Wala. His name came up in connection with the murder of Vicky Middukhera and Gurlal Brar and despite this, the police did nothing."advertisementVicky Middukhera was a Youth Akali Dal leader who was shot dead in Mohali, in August 2021. Middukhera reportedly was close to Bishnoi. The name of Shagan Preet Singh, Moose Wala’s manager, had cropped up in connection with the murder. Singh reportedly fled from India to Australia before the police could reach him. Gurlal Brar was Goldy Brar’s cousin. The Students' Organisation of Panjab University leader was killed in 2020.So, while a man named Goldy Brar has claimed responsibility for the murder of Sidhu Moose Wala, the man in the photo with Bhagwant Mann — also called Goldy Brar — has no connection with that.(Written by Yash Mittal)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: The Pied Piper of Bangladesh! Man attracting bees using flute is not devout Hindu, he’s a Muslim honey collector Just like the legendary Pied Piper of Hamelin from German folktales who was known for his ability to command rats (and children) through his tunes, a modern-day devout Hindu man allegedly has the power to sway honey bees through his flute. A video has been making the rounds of social media with this claim.Many on social media shared the video of a man dressed in yellow trunks and a saffron headband, playing the flute. A swarm of bees surrounded him, with many even sitting all over his face and body as he played a melody. Those sharing the video on Facebook and Twitter claimed that this devout man’s ability to mesmerise bees through his flute was an example of the greatness of Sanatan Dharma or Hinduism.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the man in this video is Mehtab Morol, a Muslim honey collector from Jessore, Bangladesh.The viral posts are archived here and here.AFWA ProbeEighteen seconds into the viral video, a framed photo of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, widely known as Bangabandhu, the founding father and the first president of Bangladesh, could be seen behind the man. This hinted at the video possibly being from Bangladesh.Subsequent searches with relevant keywords led us to many Bangladeshi news portals that reported this story. We also found more videos of the man on the YouTube channel of Gtv News and the Facebook page of Maasranga Television.As per these reports, the man in the video was Mehtab Morol, a professional honey collector from the Jessore district of Bangladesh. The viral clip could also be seen in the Gtv News report from June 2021.Morol, per these reports, has been collecting honey for the last twenty years. He uses several tricks associated with sound to coax bees out of their honeycombs to collect honey.“Initially, I had made sounds using different utensils to attract the bees. I used to feed the honeybees so that they would become my pet. Then I started playing the flute, and they were attracted to the tune. They don't sting me,” Morol told Gtv News.Not Sanatan DharmaTohid Moni, a journalist from Jessore who covered Morol’s story for Sarabangla and Gtv News told India Today over the phone that Morol is Muslim. Rahul Ray, another journalist from Jessore who covered this story for Maasranga Television, told us, “Mehtab is certainly a Muslim by birth. There is no Hindu connection. Honey collection is his profession. Besides the honey collection, Mehtab also shows this trick to people curious about his stunt.”To get to the bottom of the matter, we went to the horse’s mouth. When India Today got in touch with him, Morol confirmed that he is Muslim. He added, “I have been doing this experiment with honey bees since last year. This is not fake or any false trick. I have challenged people to disprove it. These bees come to me whenever I play the flute and then I feed them.”Do honey bees like the flute?advertisementDr Monowar Hossain, a Zoology professor at the Jahangirnagar University of Dhaka, Bangladesh explained to Maasranga Television, that honey bees have a fascination for particular sound wave frequencies.“The frequency of flutes attracts honey bees. Another reason is that since Mehtab feeds these bees whenever they come to him, their brains get conditioned to believe that if they move towards that particular sound, they will get food.”Thus, we confirmed that the man in the video seen attracting honey bees with his flute is a Muslim honey collector from Bangladesh called Mehtab Morol. His unique ability has been reported by several media outlets in Bangladesh.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Far from his last, this Sidhu Moose Wala interview with Sonam Bajwa is more than a year old The assassination of Punjabi singer and Congress leader Shubhdeep Singh Sidhu, better known as Sidhu Moose Wala, has shocked the nation. He was shot multiple times in the Jawaharke village of the Mansa district in Punjab on May 29.Amid fans expressing shock and grief on social media, a video of an interview featuring the Punjabi singer was shared widely with the claim that this was Moose Wala’s final interview before his death. In the video, actor Sonam Bajwa spoke to Moose Wala about his struggles in the music industry.advertisementBut was this his “last interview”? The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the video was more than a year old and was definitely not the last interview the 28-year-old musician gave.AFWA ProbeA quick search led us to the original video of the interview from March 2021 on Zee5’s website. The 42-minute long interview was from a talk show “Dil Diyan Gallan” hosted by Bajwa. In it, Bajwa and Moose Wala discussed his life, career, and music. He also addressed controversies surrounding him.The clip that is now going viral was taken from a promo video for this episode of the show that we found on the Zee Punjabi YouTube channel.This interview with Bajwa was widely reported by many news outlets. Reportedly, it was his first TV interview.Definitely not the last interviewIn the time since the now-viral interview, Moose Wala gave several others. In fact, we found two recent interviews that took place just days before his assassination.His interview with On Air was published on May 26. And the one with Lok Opinion was published on May 30, the day after his death. The video's YouTube title mentions that it was recorded a day before the tragedy, on May 28.Moose Wala lost to Aam Aadmi Party's Dr. Vijay Singla from the Mansa constituency in the recent assembly elections in Punjab. In the Lok Opinion interview, the singer said he wouldn’t be contesting elections again.Thus, we conclude that the viral clip of Sonam Bajwa interviewing Sidhu Moose Wala was not his “last interview”. He recorded interviews with news channels just days before his death.(With inputs from Yash Mittal)

content: Fact Check: ഈ വീഡിയോ പ്രധാനമന്ത്രി കുറ്റസമ്മതം നടത്തുന്നതല്ല പ്രധാനമന്ത്രി നരേന്ദ്ര മോദിയുടെ പഴയൊരു വീഡിയോ സമൂഹമാധ്യമങ്ങളിൽ പലരും പങ്കുവെക്കുന്നുണ്ട്. ചെറുപ്പത്തിൽ മോഷണങ്ങൾ ചെയ്ത് തുടങ്ങിയപ്പോൾതന്നെ തന്റെ അമ്മ അവ തിരുത്തിയിരുന്നുവെങ്കിൽ വലുതായപ്പോൾ വലിയ തെറ്റുകൾ ചെയ്യുകയില്ലായിരുന്നുവെന്ന് പ്രധാനമന്ത്രി ജനങ്ങൾക്ക് മുൻപിൽ ആത്മവിമർശനം നടത്തുന്ന രീതിയിലാണ് വീഡിയോയിലെ ഉള്ളടക്കവും തലക്കെട്ടും."ഞാൻ ചെറിയ മോഷണങ്ങൾ നടത്തിയിരുന്നപ്പോൾ എന്റെ അമ്മ എന്നെ അതിൽ നിന്ന് വിലക്കിയിരുന്നെങ്കിൽ ഞാൻ ഇത്രയും വലിയ മോഷ്ടാവ് ആകില്ലായിരുന്നു എന്ന് മോദിജി.... ഓൾഡ് വീഡിയോ ആണ് മിത്രോ ഓൾഡ് ഈസ്‌ ഗോൾഡ് എന്നല്ലേ..." എന്ന കുറിപ്പിനൊപ്പമാണ് 9 സെക്കൻഡ് ദൈർഘ്യമുള്ള വീഡിയോ പ്രചരിക്കുന്നത്.ഇന്ത്യാ ടുഡേ ആന്റി ഫേക്ക് ന്യൂസ്‌ വാർ റൂം (AFWA) നടത്തിയ അന്വേഷണത്തിൽ വാദം തെറ്റിദ്ധരിപ്പിക്കുന്നതാണെന്ന് കണ്ടെത്തി. വീഡിയോയിൽ കാണുന്നത് കള്ളനായ മകന്റെയും അമ്മയുടെയും കഥ പ്രസംഗത്തിനിടയിൽ ഉദ്ധരിക്കുന്ന പ്രധാനമന്ത്രിയെ ആണ്.AFWA അന്വേഷണംപ്രചരിക്കുന്ന വീഡിയോയുടെ പുറകിലായി കാണാവുന്ന ബിജെപി ചിഹ്നത്തിലെ ലിപി ബംഗാളി ആയിരുന്നു. ഇത് പ്രധാനമന്ത്രിയുടെ വേദി പശ്ചിമ ബംഗാൾ ആകാമെന്ന സൂചന നൽകി. ഇത് പിൻപറ്റിയുള്ള തിരച്ചിലിൽ നരേന്ദ്ര മോദിയുടെ യൂട്യൂബ് ചാനലിൽ 2021 ഏപ്രിൽ 10ന് ബംഗാളിലെ സിലിഗുരിയിൽ നടന്ന ഒരു പൊതുപരിപാടിയുടെ വീഡിയോ ലഭ്യമായി. ഈ വീഡിയോയിൽ കാണാവുന്ന വേഷവും തൊപ്പിയും ധരിച്ചുതന്നെയാണ് വൈറൽ ക്ലിപ്പിലും പ്രധാനമന്ത്രിയെ കാണാവുന്നത്.ബംഗാളിലെ നാലാംഘട്ട തെരഞ്ഞെടുപ്പിന് മുമ്പായി സിലിഗുരിയിൽ നടന്ന വമ്പിച്ച പൊതുപരിപാടി എന്നാണ് വീഡിയോയുടെ വിവരണത്തിൽ നിന്ന് വേദിയെപ്പറ്റി അറിയാനായത്. 57 മിനിറ്റ് ദൈർഘ്യമുള്ള വീഡിയോയിലെ 39ആം മിനിറ്റിൽ ഇപ്പോൾ പ്രചരിക്കുന്ന ഭാഗം കടന്നുവരുന്നത് കണ്ടെത്താൻ സാധിച്ചു.പൂർണ്ണമായ വീഡിയോ കണ്ടതിൽനിന്ന് മനസ്സിലാക്കാനായത് വൈറലായി കൊണ്ടിരിക്കുന്ന പോസ്റ്റിൽ ആരോപിക്കുന്നതുപോലെ ഇത് മോദി സ്വന്തം ജീവിതത്തെപ്രതി പറയുന്ന വാക്കുകളല്ല എന്നാണ്. കള്ളന്റെയും അമ്മയുടെയും പ്രശസ്തമായ കഥ ഉദ്ധരിച്ചുകൊണ്ട് പശ്ചിമ ബംഗാൾ മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി മമതാ ബാനർജിയെ കടന്നാക്രമിക്കുകയാണ് അദ്ദേഹമിവിടെ. ചെറുപ്പത്തിൽ ചെറിയ കളവുകൾ ചെയ്തു തുടങ്ങിയപ്പോൾ തിരുത്താതിരുന്നതിന് അമ്മയുടെ ചെവി കഴുമരത്തിലേക്കുള്ള യാത്രയ്ക്കിടയിൽ കടിച്ചുമുറിച്ച് ക്രോധം തീർത്ത കള്ളന്റെ കഥയാണ് മോദി ഇവിടെ ജനങ്ങളുമായി പങ്കുവയ്ക്കുന്നത്. ചെറുപ്പത്തിലെ തിരുത്തിയെങ്കിൽ തനിക്ക് ഈ ഗതി വരില്ലായിരുന്നു എന്ന് കള്ളൻ അമ്മയോട് പറയുന്ന രംഗമാണ് വീഡിയോയിൽ മോദി ആവർത്തിക്കുന്നത്.2021 മാർച്ചിൽ ഒരു വേദിയിൽവെച്ച് സാധാരണക്കാർ 500 രൂപയും എടുത്താൽതന്നെ പ്രശ്നമുണ്ടാക്കുന്ന ബിജെപി കോടികളാണ് അപഹരിക്കുക്കുന്നത് എന്ന മമതാ ബാനർജിയുടെ വിമർശനത്തിന് മറുപടിയായാണ് കള്ളന്റെയും അമ്മയുടെയും കഥയിലൂടെ മോദി മറുപടി പറഞ്ഞത്.If a common man steals Rs 500 then he is called a ‘tolabaaz’. Please Try Again                             മലയാളം വാർത്ത ഫാക്റ്റ് ചെക്ക്          Feedback   Fact Check: വയനാട്ടിൽ SFI പ്രവർത്തകർ ഭീകരപ്രവർത്തനം നടത്തിയെന്ന്  ഇപി ജയരാജൻ പറഞ്ഞോ - വാസ്തവമറിയാം    മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി പിണറായി വിജയനെതിരെ വിമാനത്തിൽ വെച്ച് യൂത്ത് കോൺഗ്രസ് പ്രവർത്തകർ നടത്തിയ പ്രതിഷേധത്തെ അപലപിക്കവേ ജയരാജൻ പറഞ്ഞ വാക്കുകളാണിത്.        This footage is edited, AFWA found out.           Bechu S   Thiruvananthapuram, 27 Jun 2022, (Updated 27 Jun 2022, 7:41 PM IST)                                              Follow us:ബഫർസോൺ വിഷയത്തിൽ ഇടപെടുന്നില്ല എന്നാരോപിച്ച് വയനാട് എംപി രാഹുൽ ഗാന്ധിയുടെ ഓഫീസ് എസ്എഫ്ഐ പ്രവർത്തകർ അടിച്ചു തകർത്തിരുന്നു. ഓഫീസിലേക്ക് തള്ളിക്കയറിയ പ്രവർത്തകർ ജനലുകൾ വഴി അകത്തു കടക്കുകയും ഓഫീസ് ജീവനക്കാരെ മർദ്ദിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുകയായിരുന്നു എന്നാണ് റിപ്പോർട്ടുകൾ.വിദ്യാർത്ഥി സംഘടനയ്ക്കെതിരെ വലിയ പ്രതിഷേധത്തിനാണ് ഈ സംഭവം ഇടയാക്കിയത്. കോൺഗ്രസ് ദേശീയ തലത്തിൽ വിഷയം ചർച്ച ആക്കിയപ്പോൾ സിപിഎം നേതൃത്വവും എസ്എഫ്ഐയെ തള്ളി രംഗത്തെത്തിയിരുന്നു. അക്രമത്തിന്റെ വീഡിയോകളോടൊപ്പം രാഷ്ട്രീയനേതാക്കൾ നടത്തിയ പ്രതികരണങ്ങളും സമൂഹ മാധ്യമങ്ങളിൽ പ്രചരിക്കുന്നുണ്ട്. ഇക്കൂട്ടത്തിൽ എൽഡിഎഫ് കൺവീനർ ഇപി ജയരാജന്റെ പ്രതികരണം എന്ന പേരിൽ ഒരു വീഡിയോയുമുണ്ട്. ഭീകരസംഘടനകൾ നടത്തുന്നതുപോലെയുള്ള പ്രവർത്തിയാണ് രാഹുൽഗാന്ധിയുടെ ഓഫീസ് അക്രമിച്ചതിലൂടെ എസ്എഫ്ഐ നടത്തിയതെന്ന് ഇ പി ജയരാജൻ പറയുന്നതാണ് ഇതിന്റെ ഉള്ളടക്കം. തുടർന്ന്, നാളെ അവർ ബോംബ് ഉണ്ടാക്കുകയും ഉപയോഗിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുമെന്നും, ജനാധിപത്യപരമായ സമരങ്ങളിൽ ക്ലച്ചു പിടിക്കാത്തതിനാൽ ഭീകര പ്രവർത്തനത്തിലേക്കാണ് ഇവർ നീങ്ങുന്നതെന്നും ജയരാജൻ വീഡിയോയിൽ പറയുന്നത് കേൾക്കാം. "ചിറ്റപ്പൻ പറയുന്നതിനോട് നിങ്ങൾ യോജിക്കുന്നുണ്ടോ?," എന്ന തലക്കെട്ടോടെയാണ് ഈ വീഡിയോ ഫേസ്ബുക്കിൽ പ്രചരിക്കുന്നത്.ഇന്ത്യാ ടുഡേ ആന്റി ഫേക്ക് ന്യൂസ്‌ വാർ റൂം (AFWA) നടത്തിയ അന്വേഷണത്തിൽ വാദം തെറ്റിദ്ധരിപ്പിക്കുന്നതാണെന്ന് കണ്ടെത്തി. ഈ പ്രതികരണം ഇപി ജയരാജൻ എസ്എഫ്ഐ പ്രവർത്തകർക്കെതിരെ നടത്തിയതല്ല. മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി പിണറായി വിജയനെതിരെ വിമാനത്തിൽ വെച്ച് യൂത്ത് കോൺഗ്രസ് പ്രവർത്തകർ നടത്തിയ പ്രതിഷേധത്തെ അപലപിക്കവേ ജയരാജൻ പറഞ്ഞ വാക്കുകളാണിത്.AFWA അന്വേഷണംമുഖ്യമന്ത്രി പിണറായി വിജയൻ, പാർട്ടി ജനറൽ സെക്രട്ടറി സീതാറാം യെച്ചൂരി, എൽഡിഎഫ് കൺവീനർ ഇപി ജയരാജൻ തുടങ്ങിയ സിപിഎം നേതാക്കൾ എസ്എഫ്ഐയെ വിഷയത്തിൽ തള്ളിപ്പറഞ്ഞിരുന്നു.എങ്കിലും എൽഡിഎഫ് കൺവീനർ നടത്തിയ പ്രസ്താവന ഞങ്ങൾ പരിശോധിച്ചു. അദ്ദേഹത്തിന്റെ  പ്രതികരണം യൂട്യൂബിൽ ലഭ്യമാണ്. വയനാട് എംപി രാഹുൽ ഗാന്ധിയുടെ ഓഫീസിലേക്ക് നിലവിൽ മാർച്ച് നടത്തേണ്ട ആവശ്യമുണ്ടായിരുന്നില്ല എന്നാണ് ഇപി ജയരാജൻ പറഞ്ഞത്. രാഹുൽ ഗാന്ധിയെ എൻഫോഴ്‌സ്‌മെന്റ് ഡയറക്റ്ററേറ്റ്  വേട്ടയാടുന്നതിൽ പ്രതിഷേധിച്ച് ഡൽഹിയിൽ ശക്തമായ പ്രതിഷേധങ്ങൾ നടക്കുകയാണ്. ഇ.ഡിയെ  ഉപയോഗിച്ചുകൊണ്ട് രാഷ്ട്രീയ എതിരാളികളെ നേരിടുന്ന രീതിക്കെതിരെ സിപിഎം നിലപാട് എടുക്കുമ്പോൾ അധികാരദുർവിനിയോഗം ആയി തോന്നാവുന്ന ചെയ്തികളിൽ ഏർപ്പെടാൻ പാടില്ലെന്നും വിഷയത്തിൽ പ്രതികരിക്കവെ ജയരാജൻ പറയുന്നുണ്ട്. "രാഹുല്‍ ഗാന്ധിയുടെ ഓഫീസിലേക്ക് മാര്‍ച്ച് നടത്തിയത് തെറ്റ്: ഇ.പി. ജയരാജൻ," എന്ന തലക്കെട്ടോടെ മനോരമ ന്യൂസ് ജൂൺ 24ന് യൂട്യൂബിൽ ഈ വാർത്ത നൽകിയിരിക്കുന്നത് ചുവടെ കാണാം.Advertisementഭീകപ്രവർത്തനമായോ ബോംബ് നിർമ്മാണവുമായോ ബന്ധപ്പെട്ട യാതൊരു പ്രയോഗങ്ങളും ഇവിടെ വിദ്യാർത്ഥികൾക്കെതിരെ ഇപി നടത്തിയിരുന്നില്ല. ജയരാജന്റെ വിഷയത്തിലെ മറ്റ് പ്രതികരണങ്ങളും കണ്ടെത്താനായില്ല. മീഡിയ വൺ യൂട്യൂബ് ചാനലും സമാനമായ പ്രതികരണമാണ് ഇപിയുടെതായി കൊടുത്തിരുന്നത്.'ജനാധിപത്യപരമായ സമരം ക്ലച്ചു പിടിക്കുന്നില്ല അതുകൊണ്ട് ഭീകര പ്രവർത്തനത്തിലേക്ക് നീങ്ങുന്നു' എന്ന് വൈറൽ വീഡിയോയുടെ അവസാനഭാഗത്ത് ഇപി പറയുന്നുണ്ട്. ഈ വാചകങ്ങൾ ഗൂഗിളിൽ തിരഞ്ഞപ്പോൾ ചില മാധ്യമ റിപ്പോർട്ടുകൾ ലഭ്യമായി. "മുഖ്യമന്ത്രിയെ ആക്രമിക്കാൻ കുടിപ്പിച്ച് കയറ്റിവിട്ടു; നടന്നത് ഭീകരപ്രവർത്തനം: ഇപി," എന്ന തലക്കെട്ടോടെ മലയാള മനോരമ ജൂൺ 13ന് നൽകിയിരുന്ന റിപ്പോർട്ടാണ് ആദ്യം ലഭ്യമായത്. മുഖ്യമന്ത്രിക്കെതിരെ വിമാനത്തിനുള്ളിൽവെച്ച് യൂത്ത് കോൺഗ്രസ് പ്രവർത്തകർ നടത്തിയ പ്രതിഷേധത്തെപ്പറ്റി പ്രതികരിക്കുകയായിരുന്നു ഇപി ജയരാജൻ.റിപ്പോർട്ടിന്റെ അവസാനഭാഗത്ത് ഇങ്ങനെ പറയുന്നുണ്ട്: "ഇന്ത്യയുടെ ചരിത്രത്തിൽ ഭീകരവാദികൾ മാത്രമേ ഇങ്ങനെ ചെയ്തിട്ടുള്ളൂ. പൊലീസിനെ കബളിപ്പിച്ച് വിമാനത്തിൽ കയറിയത് ഭീകരപ്രവർത്തനമാണ്. നാളെ ഇവർ ബോംബെറിയും. ജനാധിപത്യ സമരം ക്ലച്ച് പിടിക്കുന്നില്ല. അതാണ് കോൺഗ്രസ് അക്രമം നടത്തുന്നതെന്നും ഇ.പി.ജയരാജൻ പറഞ്ഞു."ഈ വരികൾക്ക് പ്രചരിക്കുന്ന വീഡിയോയിലെ പ്രതികരണവുമായി സാമ്യമുണ്ടായിരുന്നു. തുടർന്നുള്ള തിരച്ചിലിൽ ജൂൺ 13ന് തന്നെ മനോരമ ന്യൂസ് തങ്ങളുടെ യൂട്യൂബ് ചാനലിൽ നൽകിയിരുന്ന ഒരു വീഡിയോ കണ്ടെത്തി. "‘പ്രതിഷേധിച്ചവരെ ചുംബിക്കണോ? നടന്നത് ഭീകരപ്രവര്‍ത്തനം’; ന്യായീകരിച്ച് ഇ.പി.ജയരാജന്‍," എന്ന തലക്കെട്ടോടെയാണ് ഈ വീഡിയോ നൽകിയിരുന്നത്.ഇവിടെയും വിമാനത്തിനുള്ളിൽ മുഖ്യമന്ത്രിക്കെതിരെ ഉണ്ടായ പ്രതിഷേധത്തിനെതിരെയുള്ള പ്രതികരണമായിരുന്നു ഇപിയുടേത്. വീഡിയോ കണ്ടുകഴിഞ്ഞപ്പോൾ ഇപ്പോൾ പ്രചരിക്കുന്ന വീഡിയോ തന്നെയാണ് ഇതെന്ന് ഉറപ്പിക്കാനായി. എൽഡിഎഫ് കൺവീനറുടെ വാക്കുകളും ഉപയോഗിച്ചിരുന്ന കസേരയും വൈറൽ വീഡിയോയിൽ ഉള്ളതുതന്നെ ആയിരുന്നു.ഇതിൽനിന്ന് വയനാട് എംപി രാഹുൽ ഗാന്ധിയുടെ ഓഫീസിലേക്ക് അക്രമാസക്തമായി മാർച്ച് നടത്തിയ എസ്എഫ്ഐ പ്രവർത്തകർക്കെതിരെ ഇപി ജയരാജൻ നടത്തിയ പ്രതികരണം എന്ന നിലയിൽ പ്രചരിക്കുന്നത് യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി പിണറായി വിജയനെതിരെ വിമാനത്തിനുള്ളിൽ യൂത്ത് കോൺഗ്രസ് പ്രവർത്തകർ നടത്തിയ പ്രതിഷേധത്തെപ്പറ്റിയുള്ള  അദ്ദേഹത്തിന്റെ പ്രസ്താവനയാണ് ഉറപ്പിക്കാനായി.ഫാക്ട് ചെക്ക്                                           വാദം വയനാട് എംപി രാഹുൽ ഗാന്ധിയുടെ ഓഫീസിലേക്ക് അക്രമാസക്തമായി മാർച്ച് നടത്തിയ എസ്എഫ്ഐ പ്രവർത്തകർ നടത്തിയത് ഭീകരപ്രവർത്തനം ആണെന്ന് എൽഡിഎഫ് കൺവീനർ ഇപി ജയരാജൻ പറയുന്ന വീഡിയോ.     നിഗമനം ഈ വീഡിയോ കൃതൃമമായി സൃഷ്ടിച്ചതാണ്. മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി പിണറായി വിജയനെതിരെ യൂത്ത് കോൺഗ്രസ് പ്രവർത്തകർ വിമാനത്തിനുള്ളിൽ വച്ച് നടത്തിയ പ്രതിഷേധത്തെപ്പറ്റി ജയരാജൻ നടത്തിയ പരാമർശമാണിത്.         കാക്കകളുടെ എണ്ണം കളവിന്റെ തീവ്രത സൂചിപ്പിക്കുന്നു    ഒരു കാക്ക : അർദ്ധ സത്യം  രണ്ട് കാക്കകൾ : ഏറിയപങ്കും അസത്യം  മൂന്ന് കാക്കകൾ : തികച്ചും അസത്യംവസ്തുതാ  പരിശോധനക്കായി ഞങ്ങളെ ബന്ധപ്പെടാൻ ആഗ്രഹിക്കുന്നുവോ?
